articles.s: 300 global garment brands and retailers have signed the International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (International Accord) with global unions, IndustriALL and UNI, marking the highest number of signatories for any Accord agreement to date. articles.x: 300 global garment brands and retailers have signed the International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (International Accord) with global unions, IndustriALL and UNI, marking the highest number of signatories for any Accord agreement to date. These signatory brands are headquartered across 26 countries and annually source goods worth approximately USD $26 billion from Bangladesh and Pakistan. Collectively, the Accord brands source from over 2,000 factories with over 3.4 million workers in Bangladesh and Pakistan. The International Accord was renewed in 2023 as a framework agreement for a three-year term, with automatic renewal for an additional three years, making it the longest commitment in the Accord’s history. It builds upon the 2013 and 2018 Accords on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh, as well as the 2021 International Accord, each of which progressively expanded its scope and commitments. The International Accord is a legally binding agreement between global brands and trade unions, to create and maintain garment factories where no worker fears fires, building collapses or other accidents that can be prevented with reasonable health and safety measures. It promotes worker health and safety through factory inspections to identify risks; remediation to implement life-saving improvements; worker safety training to raise awareness of workers’ rights, responsibilities, and health and safety risks; and a trusted Complaints Mechanism for workers to raise health and safety concerns. The Accord Secretariat thanks all brands, trade unions and civil society organisations who have made this milestone possible. articles.s: On Monday, 7 September 2026, RMG leaders and energy experts stressed that Bangladesh must place renewable-energy transition and energy sovereignty at the centre of its long-term industrial strategy as the continuing energy crisis, rising fuel-import dependence and unreliable supply increasingly thre
articles.x: On Monday, 7 September 2026, RMG leaders and energy experts stressed that Bangladesh must place renewable-energy transition and energy sovereignty at the centre of its long-term industrial strategy as the continuing energy crisis, rising fuel-import dependence and unreliable supply increasingly threaten RMG’s sustainability. The call came at the “Rapid Energy Transition Conference: Powering Security, Sustainability and Growth in Bangladesh RMG,” convened by Ethical Trading Initiative (ETI) Bangladesh, which brought together 108 representatives from RMG factories. Speakers included representatives from BGMEA, BKMEA and BSREA, alongside international brands, financial institutions, renewable-energy companies and technical organisations. The conference featured three working sessions examining the urgency of renewable-energy transition, available financing and technology pathways, and the role of business associations in supporting industry-wide implementation, respectively. In his opening speech, Abil Bin Amin, Executive Director of ETI Bangladesh , called for a just and collaborative energy transition, stressing that factories and workers should not bear the costs of meeting international climate targets and transitioning to renewables, without collective stakeholder engagement and support. Eng. Imran Kader Turjo, Director of BKMEA , warned that Bangladesh could not secure the RMG sector’s energy future through rooftop solar alone. “We are already late; these renewable-energy and infrastructure initiatives should have been implemented 10 to 12 years ago. Our priority now must be rapid and focused implementation,” he said. articles.x: Standfirst: A visual nostalgia wave becomes economically relevant to the industrial apparel sector only when it structurally alters product design, processing chemistry and manufacturing lead times. For manufacturers, the commercial question is whether additional design complexity can be converted into value capture rather than absorbed as uncompensated operational cost. THE LONG-TERM MACRO REVIVAL: A 7-YEAR SYSTEMIC EVOLUTION The global apparel architecture is consolidating a major revival of 1980s shapes, proportions and design attitudes —a direction that has been building for several years rather than appearing as a single-season trend. To understand its significance, the timeline matters. Bangladesh has operated at global garment-manufacturing scale since the late 1970s, building its competitive position around agility, adaptability and high-volume execution. The return of stronger, more structured and volume-led product therefore does not represent an entirely foreign manufacturing challenge. The opportunity is to apply that established production base to a more technically demanding product cycle. According to WGSN Fashion Vision , wide-leg jeans—the clearest denim manifestation of the current ’80s direction—recorded a 9.4 percentage-point increase in catwalk mix compared with previous cycles, reaching a 32% share of the tracked denim mix. Historical collection tracking referenced through McKinsey Apparel Intelligence and Vogue Business also indicates that the shift away from ultra-minimal, skin-tight proportions has been developing for approximately seven to eight years . articles.x: WATTWIL, Switzerland — September 9, 2026 — Heberlein, a globally recognized provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Heberlein Air Covering Solutions Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. Other applications include stretch fabrics for trousers and jeans, elasticated cuffs, as well as medical and compression textiles. articles.o: Lycra targets the workwear market
articles.s: The Lycra Company is targeting the workwear and protective clothing market with a portfolio of fibre technologies designed to improve comfort, durability and performance in demanding working environments. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis
articles.x: The Lycra Company is targeting the workwear and protective clothing market with a portfolio of fibre technologies designed to improve comfort, durability and performance in demanding working environments. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis from September 14-16, where it will introduce its Fibers That Work portfolio to the North American market. The portfolio brings together existing and new fibre technologies for workwear, uniforms and protective apparel, addressing requirements including moisture management, visibility, antistatic protection, stretch and durability. “Comfort is fundamental to workwear performance,” says Tara Maurer-Mackay, product category director of branded specialty products at The Lycra Company. “Our innovations help workers adapt to changing conditions throughout the day with fibres that move moisture to keep them dry if they sweat, stretch that allows them to move freely, and solutions that enhance visibility for safety. “Leveraging our decades of innovation in comfort technologies, we are well positioned to help our customers create garments that workers can trust in demanding environments.” Among the technologies being highlighted is Lycra Antistatic fibre, which provides inherent antistatic properties while retaining stretch, comfort and fit. Lycra T400 fibre is meanwhile designed for durable workwear requiring comfort stretch, consistent fit and moisture management. According to the company, fabrics incorporating the fibre can withstand up to 100 industrial wash cycles. The wider Fibers That Work portfolio reflects growing demand for workwear that combines protection with greater wearer comfort and durability. articles.x: AUCKLAND – Researchers in New Zealand have found that cotton textile waste can be broken down to produce biogas. The findings raise the prospect of another end-of-life route for natural-fibre clothing that cannot be reused or recycled. The University of Auckland study tested cotton, wool and polyester-cotton blends using anaerobic digestion. This is a process already widely used to treat food waste, farm waste and sewage sludge. articles.x: ELKTON, MD — May 11, 2026 — W. L. Gore & Associates (Gore), founder of the GORE-TEX® Brand, marks 50 years of product innovation and leadership in fabrics. Since its consumer introduction in the Early Winters Light Dimension tent in 1976, Gore has expanded its portfolio into a globally trusted solution across garments, footwear, gloves. Today, GORE-TEX® Brand fabrics continue to add comfort while protecting people from everyday situations to the world’s most demanding conditions. As Gore marks this milestone, the company is not only reflecting on its legacy of innovation but also setting the course for the future. Since Bob Gore’s 1969 discovery of a lightweight, microporous material, GORE-TEX® Product technology has been driven by science-led exploration, transforming a breakthrough insight into one of the most influential materials platforms in performance fabrics. Today, that legacy continues through ongoing innovation and a commitment to advance responsible performance, the belief that performance, durability, and sustainability must advance together. These efforts span the brand’s fabrics business that extends across outdoor, professional, and defense applications, where reliable protection is critical. “For five decades, GORE‑TEX® Products have enabled people to perform in the toughest conditions,” said Michelle Augustine, Gore fabrics business leader. “We continue to build on this foundation through innovation that helps our partners meet evolving needs while advancing responsible performance for the future.” Durability has long been a focus for Gore, and the company is now bringing that commitment to the forefront, emphasizing the design of longer-lasting products to help reduce resource use while maintaining performance over time. articles.o: The Woolmark Company appoints Ismail Hossain Tushar as Technical Representative for Bangladesh
articles.s: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Busi...
articles.x: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company The Woolmark Company operates as a global authority on wool and functions as a subsidiary of Australian Wool Innovation. It drives research, technical development, and quality assurance for Australian Merino wool across international supply chains. The organization connects woolgrowers, apparel manufacturers, and global fashion brands through quality certification, technical education, and supply chain optimization. Ismail Hossain Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across the textile value chain to his new position. He holds a degree in Textile Engineering from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST). He also earned an MBA from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from the Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). His professional background includes commercial and technical positions at Shore to Shore, Groz-Beckert, Dysin Group, and Sieger Spintech. In his new role, Tushar focuses on connecting Bangladesh's manufacturing base with global wool supply chains. His work centers on providing technical support to local factories, facilitating knowledge transfer, and assisting manufacturers in developing wool and wool-blend products for export markets.

articles.s: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stan
articles.x: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stand K46, highlighting applications ranging from spacecraft heat protection to aircraft engines and structural components. BRM uses continuous 3D weaving to produce complex reinforcement structures in which fibres are integrated throughout all three dimensions of the weave. Its woven joints can be produced in a variety of shaped profiles, with the fibre architecture tailored to the load requirements of individual components. The technology is designed to provide continuous reinforcement across joined substructures, offering an alternative to conventional joining methods, and in some applications, metallic components. Using woven carbon fibre composite structures in place of metal can provide significant weight savings while maintaining the structural performance required for demanding aerospace applications. From structural joints to heat shields BRM is also applying its 3D weaving expertise to thermal protection systems for spacecraft and other extreme-temperature applications. Different yarn types, densities, thicknesses, widths and resin systems can be combined to develop woven structures for specific thermal and mechanical requirements. One of the company’s most significant developments in this field resulted from its work with NASA on 3DMAT, a three-dimensional orthogonally woven quartz material developed for compression pads on the Orion spacecraft. articles.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. — September 9, 2026 — Following the success of its inaugural 2026 event, Textiles Recycling Expo USA is inviting industry experts, innovators, researchers and thought leaders to submit speaker proposals for its 2027 conference, taking place April 7–8 at the Charlotte Convention Center, North Carolina. The call for speakers is now open as organizers begin building the program for the second edition of Textiles Recycling Expo USA, North America’s dedicated exhibition and conference focused on textile recycling and circularity. Structural Partner, Accelerating Circularity is working closely with the organizers to help identify key industry challenges and ensure the program reflects the priorities and conversations shaping the sector. Along with addressing the core continuing impact of evolving legislation, infrastructure, and technology on the textiles recycling industry, the event is also expanding their focus to explore the role of re-use and repair, and the responsibilities the US textiles industry has to countries in the global south. articles.t: 엑티브온, 키움제11호스팩과 합병 추진
articles.o: 엑티브온, 키움제11호스팩과 합병 추진
articles.s: 클린뷰티 소재 기업 엑티브온이 스팩 합병을 통한 코스닥 상장 절차에 들어갔다.엑티브온은 키움제11호스팩과 합병하는 방식으로 기업공개를 추진하기 위해 상장예비심사신청서를 제출했다고 11일 밝혔다. 2009년 설립된 엑티브온은 화장품과 퍼스널케어용 소재를 개발·생산하고 있으며, 방부·보존 솔루션과 바이오 액티브 소재, 지속가능 기능성 소재 등을 주요 사업군으로 두고 있다.회사는 정제·발효·촉매·추출·배합·변환 등 6개 기술을 기반으로 소재 사업을 전개하고 있다. 사탕수수와 팜 열매 등 바이오매스를 활용한 바이오 기반 디올 소재를 개발했

articles.t: 미미박스, 2분기 매출 50% 이상 증가…상반기 성과 인센티브 지급

articles.s: 미미박스가 상반기 경영성과를 임직원 보상과 글로벌 유통 확대로 연결하고 있다.미미박스는 2026년 상반기 경영성과를 바탕으로 임직원에게 경영성과 인센티브를 지급했다고 11일 밝혔다. 회사는 소수 핵심 제품에 판매 역량을 집중한 뒤 제품 구성과 유통 채널을 확장하는 전략을 추진하고 있다.미미박스 측에 따르면 2026년 2분기 매출은 전년 동기와 직전 분기보다 각각 50% 이상 증가했다. articles.t: 새로운 Aersulate의 유망 시장
articles.o: Promising markets for new Aersulate
articles.s: Outlast Technologies, based in Heidenheim/Brenz, Germany, is targeting sportswear and military applications for its thin, lightweight Aersulate insulation technology following encouraging initial tests with prospective customers. The German temperature management specialist developed Aersulate using
articles.x: Outlast Technologies, based in Heidenheim/Brenz, Germany, is targeting sportswear and military applications for its thin, lightweight Aersulate insulation technology following encouraging initial tests with prospective customers. The German temperature management specialist developed Aersulate using Naerogel, the aerogel material supplied by Sweden’s Svenska Aerogel, and is now in discussions with companies in both sectors over potential applications. The development follows an initial ramp-up order for Naerogel placed by Outlast with Svenska Aerogel in late 2025, suggesting the technology is moving beyond initial development towards commercial evaluation. Aerogels are highly porous, extremely lightweight materials known for their low thermal conductivity, making them attractive for applications where high levels of insulation are required without the weight and bulk associated with conventional insulating materials. In Aersulate, Outlast has incorporated Naerogel into a textile insulation designed to provide thermal protection in a thin and lightweight format. This could prove particularly relevant in performance sportswear and military clothing, where reducing garment bulk while maintaining protection from cold conditions is a continuing challenge. Initial testing for these applications has now produced positive results, according to Outlast, providing the basis for further discussions with prospective customers. “Sportswear and military products are areas where thin, lightweight insulation could offer valuable benefits,” says Martin Bentz, CEO of Outlast Technologies. “We are exploring potential applications with companies in these sectors, and the positive initial test results encourage us to pursue these opportunities further.” Specialist woven structures for aeros

articles.t: Tonello 기술로 스리랑카 허브를 강화하다
articles.o: Tonello technology powers Sri Lankan hub
articles.s: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemica
articles.x: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, Asons’ established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply sector and Tonello’s garment finishing technologies. At the centre of the facility is Tonello’s complete technology portfolio, enabling manufacturers, brands and other industry partners to develop and test washing, dyeing, laser, ozone and drying processes at a single location. The facility also incorporates Tonello’s digital process control technologies, allowing different treatments and process combinations to be evaluated, adjusted and refined before being transferred to industrial production. According to Tonello, the integrated approach enables garment manufacturers to consider chemistry, machinery and process parameters together, rather than developing individual stages of the finishing process in isolation. The hub has been conceived as a practical development environment where companies can experiment with new treatments, assess different combinations of chemicals and technologies, and develop processes capable of being scaled to commercial production. It will also provide a platform for collaboration between chemical suppliers, technology developers, manufacturers and brands seeking to improve garment finishing performance while reducing the environmental impact of production. articles.x: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers . Wattwil, Switzerland, September 9, 2026 – Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. SlideJet-FT15-2 with the APe-series Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. articles.t: 섬유에서 섬유 기회까지: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Bangladesh의 울 생태계 개발을 위한 새로운 역할 맡다
articles.o: From Textile to Fibre Opportunity: Ismail Hossain Tushar Takes on a New Role to Develop Bangladesh’s Wool Ecosystem
articles.s: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limit
articles.x: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limited. Ismail Hossain Tushar, with more than 13 years of experience across Bangladesh’s textile value chain, is taking on a new role with The Woolmark Company to explore how Bangladesh’s strong manufacturing capabilities can connect with the global wool ecosystem—and help develop a new story for wool in Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company Against this backdrop, Ismail Hossain Tushar is beginning a new professional chapter with The Woolmark Company as Business Development & Technical Representative – Bangladesh , effective 10 September 2026. But the significance of the move extends beyond a new professional appointment. At the centre of his activities will be a broader question: how can Bangladesh build a meaningful ecosystem around wool, and how can its existing textile capabilities connect with the wider global wool industry? Looking at wool through the Bangladesh textile lens Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across different areas of Bangladesh’s textile industry. A Textile Engineering graduate from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST), he later complemented his technical background with an MBA in Marketing from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). articles.o: AAFA warns against US retreat from ILO
articles.s: The Washington DC-based American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has delivered a US business community letter with 10 signatories to United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the Trump administration to put America first by restoring US funding for, and participation in the Geneva, S
articles.x: The Washington DC-based American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has delivered a US business community letter with 10 signatories to United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the Trump administration to put America first by restoring US funding for, and participation in the Geneva, Switzerland-headquartered International Labour Organization (ILO). “The ILO builds institutions in countries around the world so that they can effectively implement and enforce internationally recognised labor standards – standards the US created and upholds in its own laws,” it states. “Further, the ILO’s core international labour standards focus heavily on combatting forced labour, which is an administration priority as demonstrated by the recent Section 301 actions on forced labour and the Trump administration’s vigorous enforcement of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) and the US Forced Labor Statute (Section 1307).” The ILO maintains staff and offices in dozens of key countries that provide real time intelligence, contacts and solutions to promote and protect internationally recognised labour standards. The apparel and footwear industries, and indeed, the entire US business community, rely on the essential work of ILO, whose purpose is to work globally to ensure a level playing field for all workers, including American workers. “A US withdrawal from the ILO would cede control and leadership af the ILO to other countries who do not share American values and who instead, want to use the ILO to tilt the playing field against American businesses and American workers, de-emphasising the ILO’s focus on combatting forced labour and undermining the US-built ILO core international labour standards,” says AAFA executive vice president Nate Herman. articles.o: Archroma turns wool waste into a new generation of textile dyes
articles.s: Orta and Archroma introduce denim collection dyed with wool waste-based FiberColors. Archroma has received the 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for FiberColors, a dyeing technology that uses at least 50% w...
articles.x: Orta and Archroma introduce denim collection dyed with wool waste-based FiberColors. Archroma has received the 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for FiberColors, a dyeing technology that uses at least 50% wool waste to produce high-sulphur pigments. The innovation shows how textile waste can become a feedstock for new chemical products. The Swiss textile chemicals specialist won the award in the “Best Product Innovation from a Large Company” category. Its FiberColors technology is designed to replace some fossil-based raw materials traditionally used in dye production while giving unwanted wool a new industrial use. Wool waste can be difficult to manage when it is unsuitable for conventional textile production. Farmers may also face disposal costs for unwanted wool. FiberColors addresses this challenge by incorporating the waste into pigment synthesis for textile dyeing. According to Archroma, the FiberColors range contains at least 50% wool waste. This gives the material a role beyond disposal and creates an opportunity to retain part of the value embedded in wool. The recognition from the ICIS Innovation Awards highlights the growing importance of material innovation within the textile chemicals sector. It also signals that waste-derived raw materials are moving from experimental concepts toward commercially relevant applications. For the wider textile industry, the development offers a different way to think about circularity. Instead of treating wool waste only as an end-of-life challenge, it can be considered a potential input for producing the chemicals needed to manufacture new textile products.

articles.o: 네이처 스파, 27S/S 서울패션위크 곽현주 컬렉션 협업
articles.s: 웰니스 리커버리 브랜드 네이처 스파가 27S/S 서울패션위크 곽현주 컬렉션에 참여했다.네이처 스파는 자연 친화적인 공간 구성과 휴식을 중심으로 스파 서비스를 운영하고 있다. 브랜드 측에 따르면 지하 1,300m에서 취수한 천연 암반수를 활용한 스파 시설을 운영하고 있으며, 수분 관리와 휴식을 결합한 웰니스 경험을 주요 콘셉트로 삼고 있다.이번 협업에서는 네이처 스파의 자연·휴식 중심 콘셉트를 곽현주 컬렉션의 무대 연출과 연계했다. 패션쇼 현장에서 웰니스 요소를 접목하며 패션과 라이프스타일 분야 간 협업 범위를 넓혔다.네이처 스파 측

They lend timeless looks depth, dynamism, and an exciting tactile dimension. Whether classic striped patterns or modern solid-color interpretations, these versatile pieces pair perfectly with casual and business-casual outfits and effortlessly create a modern look. KARL MAYER’s textile product development team demonstrates just how exciting it can be to rethink structure with a collection of innovative Advanced Bubble fabrics. With their original and striking 3D effects, these extraordinary fabrics are sure to turn heads and transform even simple silhouettes into true statement pieces. A defining feature is the vertical ruffled stripes that seem to float above a delicate, transparent background. The unique look is created by the sophisticated interplay of different structures: an airy, lightweight ground with a subtle ribbed texture sets the stage for textile stripes in a trendy crinkled look, which appear on the surface like artfully appliquéd ribbons. The result is an exciting interplay of transparency, texture, and movement. These trendy outerwear fabrics can be produced on an HKS 4-M EL ECO . articles.t: Uster는 재활용 면의 다양성을 목표로 삼고 있습니다.
articles.o: Uster targets recycled cotton variability
articles.s: Uster has developed a new data-based system for assessing mechanically recycled cotton fibres and determining their suitability for different spinning processes and end uses. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix addresses one of the principal challenges in increasing the use of recycled cotton – the cons
articles.x: Uster has developed a new data-based system for assessing mechanically recycled cotton fibres and determining their suitability for different spinning processes and end uses. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix addresses one of the principal challenges in increasing the use of recycled cotton – the considerable variation in fibre quality resulting from different waste streams, recycling processes and source materials. Rather than attempting to classify recycled cotton using a single measurement, the matrix combines two fibre parameters to provide a more representative indication of likely processing behaviour and yarn quality. Its development follows extensive testing by Uster of 100% mechanically recycled cotton samples sourced from China, India and Europe. The samples covered greige, coloured and bleached fibres derived from post-industrial, pre-consumer and post-consumer textile waste. articles.x: Invest Bangladesh has prepared a draft policy to bring distressed, non-operational or closed state-owned industrial and commercial enterprises—and their unused land and facilities—back into productive economic use. The initiative seeks to increase industrial production, attract new investment and create employment opportunities. Relevant stakeholders are invited to comment on the proposed framework for transferring these assets, shares and ownership interests, or undertaking strategic divestiture through transparent and competitive processes. The deadline for submissions is 17 September 2026. 2. The proposed policy sets out an integrated framework for the proper due diligence and valuation of the relevant enterprises and assets; determination of appropriate transaction structures; attraction of domestic and foreign investors; selection of investors through a transparent and competitive process; protection of the public interest and the fair economic value of state assets; and post-transaction implementation and monitoring. 3. articles.o: Palmal Group plans new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee EPZ
articles.s: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently...
articles.x: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently held an Investment Proposal Presentation Meeting at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) headquarters for Ayesha Fashion Ltd.-2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit), marking another step toward strengthening its vertically integrated manufacturing operations. The proposed facility will expand Palmal Group’s capabilities into yarn dyeing, enabling the company to build a more integrated and efficient supply chain across its manufacturing operations. According to the company, the project will feature a fully automatic dispensing system in the laboratory along with advanced quality-testing equipment. It will also use modern low-liquor-ratio exhaust dyeing machines and a complete heat recovery system to improve energy efficiency and sustainability. The facility’s drying system will use RF dryer technology, while its planned daily finishing capacity will be approximately 15–16 tons. The planned product mix will include 70% cotton and 20% polyester. For wastewater treatment and recycling, the project will incorporate an MBR- and RO-based effluent treatment plant (ETP) system, including reject-water management. The company also plans to install an approximately 500 kWp solar power system to increase renewable energy use and improve the facility’s overall sustainability performance. Palmal Group said the investment reflects its continued focus on vertical integration, operational efficiency and sustainable growth. articles.o: Vineyard fibres used in the new Citroën C5 Aircross
articles.s: Vine branches discarded after pruning in French vineyards are being turned into interior components for the new Citroën C5 Aircross, as parent company Stellantis looks to increase its use of renewable and recycled materials. The agricultural waste is mechanically processed into fine natural fibres a
articles.x: Vine branches discarded after pruning in French vineyards are being turned into interior components for the new Citroën C5 Aircross, as parent company Stellantis looks to increase its use of renewable and recycled materials. The agricultural waste is mechanically processed into fine natural fibres and incorporated into a bio-sourced composite used for visible door panels and central console storage components. Traditionally, vine branches left after annual pruning have been treated as waste and commonly burned. The Citroën project creates an automotive application for the material while establishing a new supply chain linking the vineyards with materials specialists and vehicle component manufacturers. The development forms part of the voluntary Stellantis goal of achieving 35% green materials in its new vehicles by 2030, encompassing the increased use of recycled and renewable resources across its vehicle portfolio. Work on the vineyard fibre material dates back to 2017, when Citroën’s design team began exploring whether more natural and sustainable materials could be incorporated visibly into vehicle interiors. Research and development teams subsequently worked with a start-up specialising in vineyard fibres to determine whether the agricultural residue could meet the demanding performance and production requirements of automotive applications. The company says the resulting shorter and more localised supply chain also helps simplify logistics while creating a productive outlet for an agricultural by-product. articles.o: Lenzing invests in new debarking and chipping line at Austria headquarters
articles.s: Lenzing Group, a global leader in regenerated cellulosic fibers, is strengthening its integrated production process with a new debarking and chipping line at its pulp mill in Lenzing, Austria. Courte...
articles.x: Lenzing Group, a global leader in regenerated cellulosic fibers, is strengthening its integrated production process with a new debarking and chipping line at its pulp mill in Lenzing, Austria. Courtesy: Collected The new line replaces the existing wood processing system and is designed to improve operational efficiency, ensure consistent output and strengthen the reliability of production operations. As the first stage of the production process, efficient debarking plays a key role in maintaining consistent quality throughout pulp and fiber production. High-quality wood chips provide the foundation for producing high-quality pulp and fibers while supporting the efficient use of wood as a renewable raw material. According to Lenzing, the investment will help establish a stable and efficient production process from the initial stage of wood processing. The new debarking and chipping line strengthens the company’s integrated production system. It ensures reliable use of renewable wood resources in pulp and fiber manufacturing.

articles.t: Tranoï Tokyo가 Denim Première Vision 데뷔와 함께 돌아왔습니다.
articles.o: Tranoï Tokyo returns with Denim Première Vision debut
articles.s: Two years after its launch in 2024, Tranoï Tokyo is returning to Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo for its fifth edition this week (September 9-10), with around 200 brands from more than 25 countries taking part. This season sees the first Japanese presentation of Denim Première Vision, the internati
articles.x: Two years after its launch in 2024, Tranoï Tokyo is returning to Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo for its fifth edition this week (September 9-10), with around 200 brands from more than 25 countries taking part. This season sees the first Japanese presentation of Denim Première Vision, the international trade show dedicated to denim materials, which is staging a preview alongside Tranoï Tokyo at the same venue. The addition will bring denim manufacturers and specialists into an increasingly international mix of fashion brands and designers, with a programme spanning collections, materials, runway presentations, cultural collaborations and industry discussions. First runway show Tranoï Tokyo is staging its first runway show at the event, bringing together nine Romanian designers and Bangladesh-based Pioneer Denim. The Romanian contingent, making its fourth appearance at the event, will highlight a new generation of designers building on the country’s established textile manufacturing skills and craftsmanship while developing their own international creative identities. The runway format is intended to provide a broader perspective on contemporary Romanian fashion, presenting the designers’ work within the context of the technical and manufacturing expertise that has long supported international fashion houses. Pioneer Denim is meanwhile presenting a new collection demonstrating the potential of denim materials, manufacturing and finishing technologies. The vertically integrated company oversees production from yarn and denim fabric development through to garment manufacturing and finishing. articles.t: Zalando는 재활용 면화를 새로운 티셔츠 컬렉션에 도입했습니다.
articles.o: Zalando brings recycled cotton into new T-shirt collections
articles.s: Zalando is adding recycled cotton made from textile waste to its latest T-shirt collections. The move shows that recycled fibers are moving closer to mainstream fashion production. Figure:The T-shirt...
articles.x: Zalando is adding recycled cotton made from textile waste to its latest T-shirt collections. The move shows that recycled fibers are moving closer to mainstream fashion production. Figure:The T-shirts are made with 80% organic cotton and 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton. The European fashion retailer has partnered with Netherlands-based recycling company RE&UP Recycling Technologies. The companies are using RE&UP’s Next-Gen Cotton in five T-shirts under Zalando’s YOURTURN and Even&Odd labels. The T-shirts are made with 80% organic cotton and 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton. The recycled fiber comes from used textiles and is made for use in new textile products. This is an important step for textile-to-textile recycling. The industry has been developing technologies that can turn old clothes into new fibers. RE&UP says its technology can process cotton, polyester and polycotton textile waste. The company also aims to make its recycled fibers suitable for existing textile production systems. This can make adoption easier for manufacturers. The development also comes as brands face growing pressure to reduce textile waste and increase recycled content. Europe’s circularity rules are expected to further increase demand for recycled textile materials in the coming years. For textile manufacturers, the Zalando collection is a signal to watch the recycled fiber market closely. Demand will depend not only on sustainability claims but also on fiber quality, supply, traceability and cost. The bigger opportunity is to build a stronger textile-to-textile supply chain. More commercial orders can help connect textile collectors, recyclers, spinners, fabric makers and brands.

articles.t: Palmal Group, Adamjee EPZ의 새로운 원사 염색 유닛과의 역방향 연계 강화
articles.o: Palmal Group strengthens backward linkage with new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee EPZ
articles.s: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recentl...
articles.x: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently held an Investment Proposal Presentation Meeting at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) headquarters for Ayesha Fashion Ltd.-2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit), marking another step toward strengthening its vertically integrated manufacturing operations. Figure: Palmal Group delegates at the BEPZA Head Office presenting the investment proposal for Ayesha Fashion Ltd. – 2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit) at Adamjee EPZ. The proposed facility will expand Palmal Group’s capabilities into yarn dyeing, enabling the company to build a more integrated and efficient supply chain across its manufacturing operations. According to the company, the project will feature a fully automatic dispensing system in the laboratory along with advanced quality-testing equipment. It will also use modern low-liquor-ratio exhaust dyeing machines and a complete heat recovery system to improve energy efficiency and sustainability. The facility’s drying system will use RF dryer technology, while its planned daily finishing capacity will be approximately 15–16 tons. The planned product mix will include 70% cotton and 20% polyester. For wastewater treatment and recycling, the project will incorporate an MBR- and RO-based effluent treatment plant (ETP) system, including reject-water management. The company also plans to install an approximately 500 kWp solar power system to increase renewable energy use and improve the facility’s overall sustainability performance. articles.t: ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 로드쇼, Narayanganj 및 Dhaka에서 Bangladesh 섬유 산업과 중국 기계 부문을 함께 가져옴
articles.o: ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 Roadshows Bring Bangladesh Textile Industry and Chinese Machinery Sector Together in Narayanganj and Dhaka
articles.s: Bangladesh textile industry witnessed a strong display of interest in advanced textile machinery, technology and Bangladesh–China industrial cooperation as ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 Road Shows were held in Narayanganj on September 1 and Dhaka on September 2, bringing together around 185 participants ac
articles.x: Bangladesh textile industry witnessed a strong display of interest in advanced textile machinery, technology and Bangladesh–China industrial cooperation as ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 Road Shows were held in Narayanganj on September 1 and Dhaka on September 2, bringing together around 185 participants across the two events. The two programmes attracted textile and apparel industry leaders, business representatives, textile professionals and other stakeholders, while a four-member Chinese delegation participated in the road-show activities and interacted with Bangladeshi industry representatives. The events were organised to promote ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026, which will be held from November 20 to 24, 2026, at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), China. The exhibition is jointly owned by CEMATEX, CCPIT TEX, the China Textile Machinery Association (CTMA) and China International Exhibition Center Group (CIEC), and is positioned as a leading business platform for textile machinery in Asia. Narayanganj road show highlights industry and China cooperation The first programme was held on September 1 at the Narayanganj Club, with approximately 85 people, including Directors from BKMEA, Vice President of NCCI and Director, NCCI along with Chinese delegates and distinguished speakers. The programme began with guest arrival, registration and preliminary networking, followed by a screening of an ITMA ASIA + CITME Road Show event video. After the formal opening and prayer session, Shawkat Iqbal, Editor-in-Chief of Bangladesh Textile Journal, delivered the welcome speech. The industry perspective was presented by Ratan Kumar Saha, Director, Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), and Managing Director of P.M. Knittex Pvt. Ltd. articles.t: BYBORRE, 런던에서 DUNE 공개
articles.o: BYBORRE unveils DUNE in London
articles.s: Dutch textile innovator BYBORRE will unveil DUNE, a new 3D knitted textile collection created in collaboration with London-based design studio Raw Edges, during London Design Festival this September. The collection takes its inspiration from earthworks, crop circles, ploughed fields and patterns for
articles.x: Dutch textile innovator BYBORRE will unveil DUNE, a new 3D knitted textile collection created in collaboration with London-based design studio Raw Edges, during London Design Festival this September. The collection takes its inspiration from earthworks, crop circles, ploughed fields and patterns formed naturally in sand and snow, translating these visual references directly into knitted textile structures. DUNE combines warm, earthy neutral tones with a natural wool blend and uses three-dimensional knitting to build geometric patterns into the textile itself. The resulting surfaces have an embossed, tactile character, with depth and texture forming an integral part of the material rather than being applied as decoration. The collaboration brings together BYBORRE’s expertise in engineered knitted textiles with the experimental approach of Raw Edges, the London studio founded by designers Yael Mer and Shay Alkalay. DUNE will be presented at the WAX Building in Shoreditch as part of London Design Festival, which runs from 12–20 September 2026. The converted Victorian furniture factory is home to a group of independent British design brands and will host its WAX 2026 programme from 15–20 September. For the presentation, the new textile will be used to dress a sofa designed by Raw Edges for furniture company Cozmo. According to the London Design Festival programme, the collaboration explores how geometric patterns can be generated directly through 3D knitting, producing relief-like surfaces in which motifs are formed within the textile structure itself. The WAX Building, at 4 Garden Walk in Shoreditch, occupies four floors of a former factory once used for waxing and shellacking furniture. articles.t: VeriVide, LED 색상 평가 범위 확장
articles.o: VeriVide expands LED colour assessment range
articles.s: VeriVide has expanded its UltraView range of visual colour assessment equipment with the launch of a compact model aimed at making tuneable LED technology accessible to more organisations across textile and apparel supply chains. The Leicester-based company, a member of the British Textile Machinery
articles.x: VeriVide has expanded its UltraView range of visual colour assessment equipment with the launch of a compact model aimed at making tuneable LED technology accessible to more organisations across textile and apparel supply chains. The Leicester-based company, a member of the British Textile Machinery Association (BTMA), says the new UltraView60 provides the same colour assessment technology and functionality as its existing UltraView system, but in a smaller and more cost-effective format. The system is intended for businesses that do not require a large viewing area or where laboratory space is limited. At the same time, VeriVide has renamed its existing UltraView model as UltraView90, creating a two-model range offering different viewing areas while retaining the same core technology and capabilities. The development comes as brands, textile manufacturers, suppliers and testing laboratories increasingly move from conventional fluorescent lighting to LED technology for visual colour assessment. Consistent lighting conditions are fundamental to colour evaluation throughout textile supply chains, particularly when materials and finished products are assessed at several locations before reaching consumers. Changes in lighting technology therefore need to be introduced consistently to avoid discrepancies in colour approval between manufacturers, suppliers and their customers. VeriVide has specialised in controlled lighting and colour assessment for more than 60 years and developed the UltraView technology to provide greater flexibility as industry specifications continue to evolve. articles.t: 새로운 스리랑카 허브에 Tonello 기술 설치
articles.o: Tonello technology installed at new Sri Lankan hub
articles.s: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka. It brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, the established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply sector of Asons and Tonello’s garment finishing technologi
articles.x: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka. It brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, the established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply sector of Asons and Tonello’s garment finishing technologies. At the centre of the facility is Tonello’s complete technology portfolio, enabling manufacturers, brands and other industry partners to develop and test washing, dyeing, laser, ozone and drying processes within a single location. The facility also incorporates Tonello’s digital process control technologies, allowing different treatments and process combinations to be evaluated and refined before their implementation in industrial production. Tonello says the integrated approach will enable garment manufacturers to consider chemistry, machinery and process parameters together rather than developing individual stages of finishing in isolation. The hub has been designed as a practical development environment in which companies can experiment with new treatments, assess different combinations of chemicals and technologies and work towards processes capable of being transferred to commercial production. It will also provide a platform for collaboration between chemical suppliers, technology developers, manufacturers and brands as they seek to improve garment finishing performance while reducing the environmental impact of production. articles.o: Govt withdraws zero-duty yarn import facility to protect local textile mills
articles.s: The government has withdrawn the zero‑duty import facility for 10–30 count cotton yarn under the bonded warehouse system. The move aims to protect local textile and spinning mills. Garment manufacture...
articles.x: The government has withdrawn the zero‑duty import facility for 10–30 count cotton yarn under the bonded warehouse system. The move aims to protect local textile and spinning mills. Garment manufacturers may now import these yarn counts against a bank guarantee instead of enjoying zero duty. The National Board of Revenue (NBR) issued the gazette notification on September 7. Courtesy: Collected The decision has been welcomed by textile millers, who say it will strengthen the domestic spinning sector and reduce the leakage of bonded yarn into the local market. However, garment exporters have urged the government to reconsider the move, warning that higher yarn costs could undermine Bangladesh’s competitiveness in the global apparel market. Industry insiders said nearly 80% of Bangladesh’s annual yarn consumption falls within the 10-30 count range, with demand concentrated mainly in knitwear fabric production. Local spinners currently have the capacity to supply more than 90% of the yarn required by the export-oriented knitwear sector. Textile millers have long complained that low-priced imported yarn, along with yarn entering through informal channels from neighboring countries, has weakened the domestic textile industry. According to millers, local spinners supplied fabrics worth around $13 billion to the domestic market four to five years ago. The figure has since declined to about $9 billion, while around $4 billion worth of fabrics imported under bonded facilities is now being sold in the local market. In a statement, the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) said the decision would help local mills utilize their production capacity more effectively as demand for domestic yarn rises. articles.s: Building on its CES 2026 debut, PYIE deepens its house-of-brands strategy by announcing its association with three global technology brands at Europe’s leading consumer electronics stage PYIE, a future-ready technology and design-driven innovation ecosystem backed by the credibility, infrastructure,
articles.x: Building on its CES 2026 debut, PYIE deepens its house-of-brands strategy by announcing its association with three global technology brands at Europe’s leading consumer electronics stage PYIE, a future-ready technology and design-driven innovation ecosystem backed by the credibility, infrastructure, and legacy of Intex, today announced its brand association with three global technology and consumer product brands – Inateck, AUKEY, and ARZOPA – at IFA 2026 (Internationale Funkausstellung) in Berlin, Germany, running from September 4-8, 2026. As part of this announcement, PYIE will act as the extended arm of Inateck, AUKEY, and ARZOPA in India, bringing their global operations, products, and market presence closer to Indian consumers. The association marks a significant milestone in PYIE’s journey toward building a differentiated house of brands, bringing globally trusted technology and consumer product brands to Indian consumers. The announcement follows PYIE’s debut at CES 2026 earlier this year, where the brand first introduced its house-of-brands vision to a global audience, marked by its successful showcase and long-term partnership with Keychron, the global mechanical keyboard brand. Building on that momentum, IFA 2026 gives PYIE a platform to expand its brand portfolio and deepen its presence within the global technology and consumer electronics ecosystem. “Our association with Inateck, AUKEY, and ARZOPA is an important step in PYIE’s journey toward building a differentiated house of brands,” said Ishita Bansal, Founder and CEO, PYIE . “Each of these brands brings a distinct area of expertise, from rugged data-capture technology to award-winning charging solutions and portable display innovation. articles.o: Best of British heads to ISPO 2026 in Amsterdam
articles.s: Eleven leading British outdoor brands will come together at the new OTS Village at ISPO Amsterdam this November, creating a strong collective showcase for the UK outdoor industry on the international stage. The Outdoor Industries Association (OIA), Outdoor Trade Show (OTS), ISPO and Raccoon Media Gr
articles.x: Eleven leading British outdoor brands will come together at the new OTS Village at ISPO Amsterdam this November, creating a strong collective showcase for the UK outdoor industry on the international stage. The Outdoor Industries Association (OIA), Outdoor Trade Show (OTS), ISPO and Raccoon Media Group have been working together to create the new OTS Village at ISPO, bringing the strength of the British outdoor industry into the heart of ISPO’s new Amsterdam format and giving UK businesses a powerful platform to connect with the international sports and outdoor industry. Taking place at RAI Amsterdam from November 4-5 2026, the first edition of ISPO to be held in Amsterdam marks a new chapter for the global sports industry event. The new format is designed to bring brands, retailers, distributors, buyers, industry leaders and key communities together from across Europe and around the world, creating a more connected and commercially valuable meeting place for the industry. Brands confirmed are Berghaus, Bridgedale, Craghoppers, DMM, Keela, Montane, Mountain Equipment, Rab, Sprayway, Terra Nova Equipment and Vango. At the heart of the Village will be a central OIA and OTS area, providing a meeting and networking point and promoting not only the participating companies, but the strength and breadth of the British outdoor industry and wider outdoor economy. “We’re absolutely delighted to see the OTS Village becoming a reality,” said Andrew Denton, CEO of the Outdoor Industries Association. “Britain has an extraordinary outdoor industry, with brilliant brands, products, people and expertise, and there is something really powerful about taking that story to an international audience together.” www.theoia.co.uk The post Best of British heads to ISPO 2026 in Amsterdam appeared

articles.o: Karl Mayer lines up new technology for ITMA Asia
articles.s: Karl Mayer will address the growing pressures on Asian textile manufacturers with a wide range of new machines and textile developments at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, complemented by a major product show at its manufacturing site in Changzhou. The company will have two stands at
articles.x: Karl Mayer will address the growing pressures on Asian textile manufacturers with a wide range of new machines and textile developments at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, complemented by a major product show at its manufacturing site in Changzhou. The company will have two stands at the exhibition, with warp knitting technologies in Hall 4.1 and warp preparation developments in Hall 3. Further machine premieres will be staged by Karl Mayer China at the Changzhou site. Asia remains central to Karl Mayer’s global strategy and is home to some of the world’s most dynamic textile manufacturing markets. Producers across the region, however, are facing rising labour, energy and financing costs alongside continued price pressure from international brands. Sustainability requirements, shorter lead times and smaller production runs are adding further pressure on margins. Close to customers Karl Mayer says its latest developments have been designed specifically to address these challenges through higher productivity, greater flexibility and improved resource efficiency. Karl Mayer CEO Lutz Wolf. © Karl Mayer “Our closeness to customers in Asia helps us identify market requirements at an early stage and translate them into targeted innovations,” says Karl Mayer CEO Lutz Wolf. “At this trade fair, we will be showcasing solutions that are not only technologically leading, but above all, deliver measurable added value and long-term growth opportunities for our customers.” Warp knitting In warp knitting, Karl Mayer will introduce a new generation of tricot machines building on the cost-effective range that has proved particularly successful in China from the late 2010s onwards. articles.o: Bengaluru’s first ‘Circular Textile Lab’ aims to prevent textile waste from reaching landfills
articles.s: A first-of-its kind Circular Textile Lab aims to prevent ‘virgin textile waste’ from reaching the landfills. The lab will convert textile discards into useful and creative products through a circular, skills-based approach, train women from underprivileged communities and provide opportunities to de
articles.x: A first-of-its kind Circular Textile Lab aims to prevent ‘virgin textile waste’ from reaching the landfills. The lab will convert textile discards into useful and creative products through a circular, skills-based approach, train women from underprivileged communities and provide opportunities to develop sustainable livelihoods by reusing and transforming textile waste. An initiative of Bengaluru South City Corporation, the city’s first Circular Textile Lab and Solid Waste Management (SWM) Learning Centre, will be inaugurated at the ward-level integrated SWM Centre, in Koramangala on Monday, aimed at promoting sustainable waste management and reducing the amount of waste sent to landfills. The Circular Textile Lab, located in the same facility, will address the growing problem of virgin textile waste reaching landfills. Photo | EPS The SWM Learning Centre is being established as a practical learning and capacity-building facility for school and college students, citizens, corporate employees, government personnel, NGOs and SWM workers. Located within an operational waste management facility that processes 18 tonnes of different waste streams daily, the centre will combine classroom learning with first-hand exposure to waste processing. Through interactive programmes, demonstrations, games and facility tours, participants will learn about waste segregation, the seven R’s of sustainability, composting, dry and reject waste management, zero-waste campuses and events, and ways to reduce waste at source. The Circular Textile Lab, located in the same facility, will address the growing problem of virgin textile waste reaching landfills. articles.t: Pangaia, Fulgar 원사 선택 갱신
articles.o: Pangaia renews Fulgar yarn choice
articles.s: Pangaia has renewed its collaboration with Italian yarn producer Fulgar, selecting its EVO bio-based yarn for the international brand’s Seamless Activewear Fall-Winter 2026 collection. The new collection is the first to be developed by Pangaia’s Milan-based design studio and sees EVO return as one o
articles.x: Pangaia has renewed its collaboration with Italian yarn producer Fulgar, selecting its EVO bio-based yarn for the international brand’s Seamless Activewear Fall-Winter 2026 collection. The new collection is the first to be developed by Pangaia’s Milan-based design studio and sees EVO return as one of the key materials in the activewear capsule, following its use in the line introduced in 2025. The continued partnership reflects Pangaia’s confidence in the performance characteristics of Fulgar’s 100% bio-based yarn, which has been developed to meet growing demand for high-performance materials produced from renewable resources. EVO is produced from 50% renewable feedstocks, including castor oil sourced from crops grown on arid land that does not compete with food production, and 50% industrial corn not intended for human consumption. According to Fulgar, the resulting yarn combines lightweight comfort and technical performance with the use of renewable raw materials. The yarn’s properties are particularly suited to activewear applications. Lightweight, breathable, elastic and quick-drying, EVO enables garments to move naturally with the body while providing effective compression, softness and freedom of movement. Its thermoregulating and bacteriostatic properties are also designed to support lasting wearer comfort. © Fulgar These characteristics have been incorporated into Pangaia’s latest Seamless Activewear capsule, which represents an evolution of the collection first introduced in 2025. The Fall-Winter 2026 range features more refined construction, graduated compression and an enhanced second-skin fit designed to support natural body movement. articles.t: 네덜란드 대사관 대표단, 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd 방문
articles.o: Netherlands Embassy delegation visits 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd
articles.s: Strengthening Partnerships for a Sustainable & Responsible Garment Industry 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., a LEED Platinum-rated green factory of TEAM Group, welcomed a high-level delegation from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, Solidaridad Network Asia, and Fair Wear Foundation to
articles.x: Strengthening Partnerships for a Sustainable & Responsible Garment Industry 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., a LEED Platinum-rated green factory of TEAM Group, welcomed a high-level delegation from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, Solidaridad Network Asia, and Fair Wear Foundation today. The delegation included Mrs. Janna van der Linden, Deputy Ambassador and Head of Trade & Development Cooperation, alongside representatives from the Embassy, Solidaridad Network Asia and Fair Wear Foundation. The delegation was welcomed by Mr. Abdullah Hil Nakib, DMD, TEAM Group, together with the leadership team of 4A Yarn Dyeing and TEAM Group Sustainability. During the visit, the delegation explored 4A’s approach to responsible business, sustainable manufacturing, digital transformation, environmental performance, decarbonisation efforts, implementing circular economy, and preparedness for evolving EU regulatory requirements. The visit reflects the growing importance of collaboration among industry, development partners and stakeholders in advancing responsible, competitive and sustainable garment manufacturing in Bangladesh. TEAM Group remains committed to going beyond compliance—building a resilient, responsible and future-ready textile industry. The post Netherlands Embassy delegation visits 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd appeared first on Textile Focus .

articles.s: 폴리에스터 감량물 전문기업 신일텍스가 고급화한 감량물 소재를 앞세워 유럽과 미국 등 글로벌 시장 공략에 나섰다.신일텍스는 프랑스 파리에서 열린 26PV(Première Vision Paris)에 참가해 글로벌 패션시장에서 요구되는 폴리에스터 감량물 소재와 다양한 신제품을 선보이며 해외 바이어들과 상담을 진행했다.신일텍스가 주력하는 분야는 폴리에스터 감량물이다. 과거에는 폴리에스터 소재에 프린트를 접목한 제품도 다양하게 전개했지만, 최근에는 감량 가공을 기반으로 소재 자체의 촉감과 표면감, 외관을 차별화하는 데 역량을 집중하고 있다.

articles.t: 印, 유니클로에 현지 투자·소싱 확대 요청
articles.o: 印, 유니클로에 현지 투자·소싱 확대 요청
articles.s: 인도 정부가 유니클로를 비롯한 일본 섬유 · 패션기업을 상대로 현지 투자와 인도산 제품 소싱 확대를 독려하고 있다. 일본 기업의 인도 내 판매 확대에 그치지 않고, 인도에서 생산된 의류와 섬유제품을 일본과 글로벌 유통망에 공급하는 소싱 기반을 넓히겠다는 구상이다.피유시 고얄 인도 상공부 장관은 지난달 24~27일 일본을 방문해 유니클로 모회사 패스트리테일링의 야나이 다다시 회장 겸 최고경영자(CEO)를 비롯한 일본 기업 경영진과 투자 확대 방안을 논의했다. 특히 유니클로와의 협의에서는 인도 내 소매사업 확대와 함께 제조 및 지속가능

articles.o: BTMA Statement on De-bonding of 10–30 Count Cotton Yarn Imports
articles.s: In light of the decision of the Inter-Ministerial Committee formed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the National Board of Revenue (NBR), through Order No. 51/2026/Customs/519 dated 7 September 2026, has withdrawn Bond facilities for the import of 10–30 count cotton yarn under HS Headings 5205, 5206 an
articles.x: In light of the decision of the Inter-Ministerial Committee formed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the National Board of Revenue (NBR), through Order No. 51/2026/Customs/519 dated 7 September 2026 , has withdrawn Bond facilities for the import of 10–30 count cotton yarn under HS Headings 5205, 5206 and 5207 . At the same time, genuine exporters have been allowed to import such yarn subject to prescribed conditions and the submission of a Bank Guarantee . The Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) considers this decision timely and appropriate to protect the domestic textile industry, particularly the spinning sector, and to prevent misuse of the Bond facility. BTMA sincerely appreciates and thanks the Government and the National Board of Revenue for taking this important initiative. 1. Revitalizing the Domestic Textile and Spinning Sector The import of yarn under Bond facilities has, for a long time, affected the demand for locally produced 10–30 count cotton yarn and limited the utilization of domestic spinning mill capacity. The new decision is expected to increase demand for locally produced yarn, create opportunities for closed and partially closed mills to resume operations, generate significant employment, and improve prospects for recovering investments made by banks and financial institutions. It is also expected to significantly reduce non-performing loans (NPLs) in the banking sector. 2. Increasing Value Addition and Conserving Foreign Currency Greater use of domestically produced yarn will significantly increase local value addition across the textile and RMG value chain while reducing foreign currency expenditure on imported yarn. articles.s: 국내 화장품 시장의 진입 문턱은 낮아졌지만 성장 문턱은 오히려 높아지고 있다. OEM·ODM 산업의 발달로 자체 생산시설 없이도 브랜드를 출시할 수 있게 되면서 시장에 뛰어드는 사업자는 급증했지만, 실제 일정 규모 이상으로 성장하는 과정에서는 자본과 유통, 물류, 마케팅 역량의 중요성이 더 커지고 있다.식품의약품안전처 등에 따르면 국내 화장품 책임판매업체 수는 2025년 2만8412개로 집계됐다. 같은 기간 화장품 제조업체는 4158개로 집계됐다.시장 참여자가 빠르게 늘어난 것과 달리 산업 자체의 성장 속도는 상대적으로 완만했다.

articles.t: Palmal Group, Sylhet에 지속 가능한 주력 복합소재 공장 개발
articles.o: Palmal Group to develop flagship sustainable composite factory in Sylhet
articles.s: Palmal Group is developing Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. at Sreehatta Economic Zone, Sylhet. The flagship composite facility marks a major investment in sustainable, future‑ready manufacturing for Ban...
articles.x: Palmal Group is developing Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. at Sreehatta Economic Zone, Sylhet. The flagship composite facility marks a major investment in sustainable, future‑ready manufacturing for Bangladesh. The new facility is being designed with sustainability at its core, with an ambition to achieve LEED Platinum certification. It will incorporate advanced technologies aimed at improving energy and water efficiency, reducing emissions and minimizing environmental impact. Figure 1: Land Lease Agreement Handed over to Palmal Management by Invest Bangladesh Authority, IBA. The planned factory will feature rooftop solar power generation, biomass boilers and an advanced Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) with water recycling facilities. It will also use energy- and water-efficient machinery, low-emission technologies and other sustainable manufacturing solutions. The Land Lease Agreement for the project was formally signed and handed over by Saleh Ahmed, Executive Member (Investment Development), BEZA and Additional Secretary, to Adnan Imtiaz Majid, Director, Central Management, Palmal Group. Figure 2: Officials from the companies/ The new facility is expected to further strengthen Palmal Group’s manufacturing capabilities while supporting its broader commitment to responsible production, resource efficiency and environmental sustainability. With sustainability integrated into the project from its foundation, Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. is expected to emerge as a benchmark for green and resource-efficient manufacturing in Bangladesh. The investment reflects Palmal Group’s continued efforts to develop modern manufacturing infrastructure that combines industrial growth with environmental responsibility.

articles.s: 대웅FNT(대표 박시우)가 스트레치 소재를 중심으로 한 자체 기술력과 특허 개발품을 앞세워 글로벌 시장 개척에 속도를 내고 있다.국내 생산 기반과 폭넓은 설비 경쟁력을 바탕으로 기능성 소재를 개발하고, 유럽을 비롯한 해외 시장에서 차별화된 경쟁력을 확보한다는 전략이다.대웅FNT는 스트레치 소재를 주력 아이템으로 전개하고 있으며, 특히 기능성과 착용감을 중시하는 해외 시장을 중심으로 수출 비중을 크게 확대해 왔다. 과거 내수 중심의 사업구조에서 현재는 내수 비중이 약 10% 수준까지 낮아지고 수출 중심으로 사업 포트폴리오가 전환됐다.

articles.x: Dr. Aminul Haque, an internationally experienced business leader, supply chain strategist, and technology transformation expert, brings more than two decades of global experience spanning strategy, operations, supply chain, and innovation. Having held senior leadership positions in globally respected multinational organizations, he has built a distinguished track record of driving business transformation, sustainable growth, and operational excellence. His expertise in blockchain, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, sustainability, and global supply chain management positions him as a leading voice on the future of transparency, technology, and responsible growth in the fashion and textile industry. articles.o: Chinese Manufacturing Is Coming to Bangladesh. Can Dhaka Turn It Into Industrial Power?
articles.s: The arrival of Chinese manufacturers could help Bangladesh diversify beyond RMG and reduce some import dependence—but without local suppliers, skills, and technology transfer, the country may simply become another assembly base in China’s global supply chain For decades, Bangladesh’s economic relati
articles.x: The arrival of Chinese manufacturers could help Bangladesh diversify beyond RMG and reduce some import dependence—but without local suppliers, skills, and technology transfer, the country may simply become another assembly base in China’s global supply chain For decades, Bangladesh’s economic relationship with China has been remarkably simple: China makes, Bangladesh imports . That relationship is now taking on another dimension. Chinese manufacturers are increasingly exploring production in Bangladesh, particularly in textiles and apparel, while Chinese businesses already have a significant presence in infrastructure, energy, telecommunications and other industrial activities. The significance goes well beyond the value of individual factory investments. Bangladesh exported US$48.28 billion in merchandise in FY2024-25, according to the Export Promotion Bureau, of which US$39.35 billion came from RMG . At the same time, China remains Bangladesh’s largest import source, with Bangladesh importing roughly US$24 billion worth of goods from China in FY2023-24 against exports of around US$1 billion . In other words, Bangladesh’s trade relationship with China carries a deficit of roughly US$23 billion . Chinese manufacturing investment could change that equation—from China selling to Bangladesh to China investing in Bangladesh to produce for Bangladesh and the world . But whether that is a transformation or simply a change of location depends on how much of the resulting value Bangladesh can retain. The investment opportunity is bigger than RMG The obvious entry point is apparel. articles.o: Nordic apparel market makes traceability a sourcing priority
articles.s: Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden) are becoming an important testing ground for Europe’s textile transition. Traceability is moving from a sustainability goal to a sourci...
articles.x: Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden) are becoming an important testing ground for Europe’s textile transition. Traceability is moving from a sustainability goal to a sourcing requirement. Figure: Global fiber production reached 132 million tons in 2024. Less than 1% came from pre- and post-consumer textile recycling. The EU launched its Digital Product Passport (DPP) Registry on 20 July 2026. Textile-specific requirements are expected to follow under the EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation. The rules are expected to require data on fiber content, recycled materials, material origin, chemicals, durability and end-of-life options, according to the European Commission. Nordic brands are already preparing. H&M Group sourced from nearly 800 apparel factories in 23 countries and about 550 raw-material factories in 15 countries as of February 2026. In 2025, 91% of its materials were recycled or sustainably sourced. Recycled materials reached 32%, above its 30% target, according to H&M Group. Supplier certification is also growing. Almost 50% of H&M’s contracted apparel factories had Recycled Claim Standard certification. Another 39% had Global Recycled Standard certification. About 38.5% had Organic Content Standard certification, according to Shenglu Fashion. The focus is also moving deeper into the supply chain. Danish brand GANNI plans to cover all Tier 1, Tier 1+ and Tier 2 suppliers through social audits or assessments by 2028, according to GANNI’s 2026 sustainability strategy. This creates a clear message for global suppliers. Traceability will increasingly influence market access and sourcing decisions. articles.o: RE&UP cotton powers Zalando collection
articles.s: RE&UP Recycling Technologies’ Next-Gen Cotton is being used in a new collection from Zalando’s private labels, marking a further step towards bringing textile-to-textile recycled fibres into mainstream commercial fashion production. Launched on Zalando in August, the collection comprises five T-shir
articles.x: RE&UP Recycling Technologies’ Next-Gen Cotton is being used in a new collection from Zalando’s private labels, marking a further step towards bringing textile-to-textile recycled fibres into mainstream commercial fashion production. Launched on Zalando in August, the collection comprises five T-shirts across YOURTURN by Zalando and Even&Odd by Zalando. The garments are made from a circular knitted fabric combining 80% organic cotton with 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton, a recycled fibre produced from textile waste. The collection marks the first time RE&UP recycled fibres have featured in Zalando’s private label assortment and demonstrates how textile-to-textile recycling technologies can move beyond pilot projects into commercial-scale applications. As the fashion industry seeks to scale textile-to-textile recycling, RE&UP says it is developing the infrastructure required to support larger volumes and enable brands to integrate next-generation fibres into existing supply chains without compromising product quality. RE&UP’s proprietary recycling process transforms pre- and post-consumer textile waste through sorting, deconstruction and decolourisation. The resulting recycled materials are designed to meet the technical, performance and traceability requirements of commercial textile manufacturing. “Industrial-scale circularity is no longer aspirational but operational,” said Özgür Atsan, Chief Commercial Officer of RE&UP. “Through collaborations like this, brands can move from pilot projects to repeatable, scalable production with confidence.” Zalando says the project demonstrates the potential for next-generation materials to meet the commercial and quality requirements of its private label businesses. “Zalando’s Private Label brands are where entry price points, quality and
