articles.t: 업계 리더들, 65번째 Dornbirn GFC 개장
articles.o: Industry leaders to open 65th Dornbirn GFC
articles.s: The 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress (Dornbirn GFC) will open on September 16th in the Austrian town, with a high-level programme bringing together senior representatives from across the European fibres, textiles and nonwovens industries to address the technological, regulatory and economic force
articles.x: The 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress (Dornbirn GFC) will open on September 16 th in the Austrian town, with a high-level programme bringing together senior representatives from across the European fibres, textiles and nonwovens industries to address the technological, regulatory and economic forces reshaping the sector. Beginning at 9am in Hall A, the opening session will set the scene for the congress with perspectives on innovation, sustainability, circularity, European competitiveness and the continuing transformation of the fibre industry. Managing director of the congress, Béatrice Moureaux will officially open proceedings before Robert van de Kerkhof, president of the Austrian Fibers Institute, addresses the importance of innovation and the methodologies increasingly influencing the direction of the textile industry. A former Lenzing board member with extensive international experience in fibres and sustainability, van de Kerkhof will examine how developments including the European Green Deal and Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) methodology are helping shape future priorities for the industry. Demanding objectives The European fibre sector’s changing competitive environment will provide another major focus of the morning. Elke Hortmeyer of the Bremen Cotton Exchange will consider the challenges facing European fibres as the industry seeks to reconcile international competitiveness with increasingly demanding sustainability objectives, while Frédéric van Houte of CIRFS, the European Man-made Fibres Association, will provide the perspective of Europe’s man-made fibre producers. articles.o: PI Cottex builds on Brückner stenter investments
articles.s: India’s PI Cottex is planning further investment in finishing technology as it looks to increase production capacity from around 600 to 1,000 tons per month over the next two-to-five years. The Ludhiana-based company already operates four stenters, including two supplied by Brückner, one a six-chamb
articles.x: India’s PI Cottex is planning further investment in finishing technology as it looks to increase production capacity from around 600 to 1,000 tons per month over the next two-to-five years. The Ludhiana-based company already operates four stenters, including two supplied by Brückner, one a six-chamber system and the other with ten-chambers, and says its experience with the German machinery manufacturer is encouraging it to consider further installations as part of its expansion plans. “The reliable performance, high process reliability and consistently high quality of the finishing results gave us the confidence to invest in Brückner technology again,” says PI Cottex managing director Jasdeep Singh. He points in particular to the dryer design of the Brückner machines, which enables certain processes to be carried out with fewer chambers while maintaining the required results. Other benefits include high production output, consistent heat-setting, improved shrinkage control and reduced energy consumption. Control parameters The investments form part of the continuing development of PI Cottex from a traditional contract finisher into a vertically integrated knitted fabric manufacturer. The company now carries out knitting, dyeing and finishing in-house, providing control over parameters including colour shade, fabric weight and width, shrinkage and hand feel. Its portfolio includes single jersey, piqué, terry, fleece, rib, interlock and waffle fabrics, along with activewear materials, primarily based on cotton and cotton-elastane blends. It also develops fabrics to individual customer requirements in terms of weight, width, fibre blend, colour and finish. articles.o: Avantex Fashion Pitch names finalists
articles.s: Ten innovators developing new technologies, materials and business models for the fashion and textile industries have been selected as finalists for the ninth Avantex Fashion Pitch. The international competition, organised by Messe Frankfurt France, culminates on 31 August 2026 with a Grand Finale i
articles.x: Ten innovators developing new technologies, materials and business models for the fashion and textile industries have been selected as finalists for the ninth Avantex Fashion Pitch. The international competition, organised by Messe Frankfurt France, culminates on 31 August 2026 with a Grand Finale in the Agora at Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris. The finalists will present their solutions before a jury comprising investors, industry professionals and fashion innovation specialists. An evening event at Le Balcon, the rooftop restaurant of Galeries Lafayette, will bring together finalists, jury members, partners and invited guests, culminating in the announcement of the 2026 Avantex Fashion Pitch winner. Messe Frankfurt France launched Avantex Fashion Pitch alongside its Avantex Paris trade show to identify emerging solutions with the potential to transform how fashion is designed, manufactured and consumed, while helping their developers gain industry visibility and accelerate growth. The competition is open to start-ups, innovative SMEs, NGOs, researchers and entrepreneurs developing products, services and technologies for the fashion and textile industries, with a particular emphasis on B2B and B2B2C business models. This year’s finalists span services, textile and raw material innovation, and design technologies. YAWYA, founded by Shikha Shah, is developing a body-scanning solution combined with an automated fitting service aimed at helping designers deliver bespoke fashion. Seconde Matière, led by Angela Hertault, operates a B2B marketplace designed to facilitate the sourcing, resale and management of surplus textiles, leather and fashion components. articles.o: Smarter and more connected at ITMA 2027
articles.s: On September 24th 2026 at 10am, the organisers of the ITMA 2027 textile machinery show will hold a live webinar entitled From Connected Factories to Competitive Advantage. As technology connects, more machines, processes, data and people across the factory, the next challenge is turning that connect
articles.x: On September 24 th 2026 at 10am, the organisers of the ITMA 2027 textile machinery show will hold a live webinar entitled From Connected Factories to Competitive Advantage. As technology connects, more machines, processes, data and people across the factory, the next challenge is turning that connectivity into real business advantage. Industry leaders will explore how automation and digital innovation can improve productivity, quality, agility and operational resilience, and how manufacturers can make smarter technology investment decisions. Participants can register here . The rise of the intelligent garment factory is meanwhile the subject of the latest ITMA Blog. Automation challenge Walk into one of today’s large apparel factories and you’ll witness autonomous vehicles, intelligent transport systems, automated warehouses, machine vision and AI-driven production planning. Yet at the centre of all this technology remains a surprisingly familiar sight – banks of operators guiding fabrics through sewing machines. Joining two pieces of textile together continues to be one of manufacturing’s hardest automation challenges. Unlike steel, plastic or other rigid materials, fabrics stretch, wrinkle, distort and behave differently depending on their construction, weight and finish. Humans instinctively compensate for these variations. Robots still struggle. As a result, sewing remains the most labour-intensive stage of garment production and depending on the complexity of the products being made, typically accounts for between 30-50% of the workforce within a vertically integrated garment factory, according to industry studies by Better Work, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and apparel manufacturing researchers. articles.s: OBERTSHAUSEN, Germany — September 1, 2026 — At ITMA ASIA in Shanghai, KARL MAYER will once again demonstrate that it understands the challenges facing the Asian textile industry – and will present tailor-made solutions. It will do so across no fewer than three stages: Hall 4.1, Booth C18 for warp kn
articles.x: OBERTSHAUSEN, Germany — September 1, 2026 — At ITMA ASIA in Shanghai, KARL MAYER will once again demonstrate that it understands the challenges facing the Asian textile industry – and will present tailor-made solutions. It will do so across no fewer than three stages: Hall 4.1, Booth C18 for warp knitting Hall 3, Booth A24 for warp preparation An accompanying mega Product Show at the company’s Changzhou site The Asian markets are among the most dynamic and innovative in the world and are a key part of KARL MAYER’s global strategy. Across Asia, rising labour, energy, and financing costs are compounded by continued price pressure from international brands. At the same time, sustainability requirements, shorter lead times, and smaller batch sizes are making the battle for margins even tougher. With its new machines and textile solutions for ITMA ASIA, KARL MAYER will directly address precisely these challenges. “Our closeness to customers in Asia helps us identify market requirements at an early stage and translate them into targeted innovations. That is why, at this trade fair, we will be showcasing solutions that are not only technologically leading but, above all, deliver one key benefit: they create measurable added value and long-term growth opportunities for our customers,” explains Lutz Wolf, CEO of KARL MAYER. The company will present its solutions to the challenges facing its customers at two exhibition booths in Shanghai. This approach will also allow KARL MAYER to engage with customers from both the warp knitting and warp preparation sectors within their own industry environment. articles.t: Kapoor Industries, Biancalani AIRO®24 제품군을 8대 기계로 확장
articles.o: Kapoor Industries Expands Biancalani AIRO®24 Fleet to Eight Machines
articles.s: The Indian terry product manufacturer’s repeat investment highlights the role of finishing performance and local technical support in building long-term machinery partnerships. Kapoor Industries Limited has expanded its installed base of Biancalani AIRO®24 finishing machines to eight units across it
articles.x: The Indian terry product manufacturer’s repeat investment highlights the role of finishing performance and local technical support in building long-term machinery partnerships. Kapoor Industries Limited has expanded its installed base of Biancalani AIRO®24 finishing machines to eight units across its manufacturing facilities in India. The repeat investment represents a significant milestone for Italian textile machinery manufacturer Biancalani and strengthens its position in the Indian textile finishing market. Kapoor Industries is one of India’s established manufacturers and exporters of premium terry products, including towels, bath mats, rugs and bathrobes. The company operates vertically integrated manufacturing facilities in Panipat and supplies international customers, primarily in the United States and Europe. As Kapoor Industries has expanded its production capacity, it has continued investing in the AIRO®24 platform to support the finishing requirements of its terry product lines. While an initial machine order can demonstrate interest in a particular technology, repeated investment provides a stronger indication of its performance under industrial production conditions. The presence of eight AIRO®24 machines suggests that the technology has delivered consistent results across multiple stages of Kapoor Industries’ expansion. AIRO®24 Supports Terry Fabric Finishing Biancalani’s AIRO®24 is designed for continuous, open-width tumble drying, softening and finishing of woven, knitted and nonwoven fabrics. The system uses controlled high-speed airflow to move fabric alternately through a treatment channel and against specially designed stainless-steel grids. articles.t: Schotex Global®, 북유럽 영업 이사로 Mats Jengard 환영
articles.o: Schotex Global® Welcomes Mats Jengard As Nordic Sales Director
articles.s: HONG KONG — September 1, 2026 — Sustainable and high-performance textile and textile technology developer Schotex Global® Co. Ltd. announces it has named outdoor industry sales veteran Mats Jengard as its head of sales for the Nordic region. Jengard brings more than 25 years of successful sales and
articles.x: HONG KONG — September 1, 2026 — Sustainable and high-performance textile and textile technology developer Schotex Global® Co. Ltd. announces it has named outdoor industry sales veteran Mats Jengard as its head of sales for the Nordic region. Mats Jengard Jengard brings more than 25 years of successful sales and project management experience to his position at Schotex. Based in Sweden, Jengard has served as sales manager for established outdoor performance brands, including Norrona, PrimaLoft and W.L. Gore & Associates. Designed in Switzerland, developed from European raw materials, and manufactured on European machinery, the Schotex Global collection pairs Swiss design heritage with the efficiency of Asian manufacturing. Schotex Global textiles range from its ACTIVE double weave constructions and FLEX single-layer textiles with exceptional 4-way stretch comfort to its TERRA natural fiber and technical synthetic blends and its SHIELD ultimate weather protection 2- or 3-layer laminates. “We see great potential for Schotex in Northern Europe with the addition of Mats to our team, and are excited for him to introduce our product offerings to the outdoor performance brands in his Nordic region,” said Schotex Co-Founder and CEO Gwen Hsu. “His deep experience with global brands, collaborative work style, and focus on guiding long-term partnership programs with exceptional customer service align perfectly with our company goals and working principles. He is also a passionate outdoorsman who understands exactly what our consumers need and look for in their garments.” Outside of work, Jengard enjoys alpine skiing, downhill biking, hiking, as well as golf. He resides in Trollhättan, Sweden, with his wife of 30 years, their kids and dog. Posted: September 1, 2026 Source: Schotex Gl

articles.o: Tiger Group Sells Fabrication And Assembly Equipment From Two U.S. Manufacturing Plants
articles.s: LOS ANGELES — September 1, 2026 — Tiger Commercial & Industrial (C&I) has completed the sale of a portfolio of high-precision fabrication and assembly machinery and equipment (M&E), along with finished products and raw materials, from two U.S. plants. Conducted on behalf of the secured creditors, th
articles.x: LOS ANGELES — September 1, 2026 — Tiger Commercial & Industrial (C&I) has completed the sale of a portfolio of high-precision fabrication and assembly machinery and equipment (M&E), along with finished products and raw materials, from two U.S. plants. Conducted on behalf of the secured creditors, the online auction featured M&E from the former Alpharetta, Georgia, and Dallas, Texas, facilities of Auzmet, a national manufacturer of exterior building solutions such as composite metal panels, architectural façades and insulated wall panels. Schlebach Quadro+ standing seam rollforming system Tiger marketed a broad mix of equipment from the two facilities, including CNC routers, electro-mechanical plate shears, CNC folding machines, electro-pneumatic saws, and smart routers by brands such as Miller, Lincoln Electric, FomIndustrie, Schechtl and Schlebach. Bidders in the 415-lot sale vied for plant-support M&E and rolling stock by brands such as Kaesar, Chevy and Mitsubishi, along with raw materials and finished-goods inventory originally valued at more than $1 million. Tiger’s in-house auction and operations team leveraged its proprietary database of repeat buyers in composites manufacturing to drive demand across the offering, managing the entire sale and removal process across both facilities within a tight 30-day deadline set by the landlord. “Our years of experience with aluminum fabrication equipment—including large-format panel builders from AXYZ Automation Group and units from Schechtl and Durma—gave us the ability to execute and quickly monetize the collateral,” said Jonathan Holiday, Senior Director of Tiger Commercial & Industrial. “The end result was a robust recovery for the secured creditors in a fraction of the usual timeframe.” Posted: September 1, 2026 Source:

Part of the diversified Balavigna Group of Companies, the company has manufacturing divisions in weaving, home textiles and garments, industrial fabrics, and weaving preparatory and wider-width fabrics, all located in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu. Prabhu, Founder & Executive Director During an exclusive interaction at the company’s booth at the recently held Bharat Tex 2026 trade fair, Dr. M. Recalling the company’s humble beginnings, he said, “I am a first-generation entrepreneur. When we started, we had a turnover of around Rs. 24 lakh per annum. articles.o: Germany faces a circularity challenge as textile waste rises
articles.s: Germany’s textile recycling sector is facing growing pressure as rising textile waste, contamination and weaker reuse markets challenge the country’s circular economy. Recyclers are struggling with hi...
articles.x: Germany’s textile recycling sector is facing growing pressure as rising textile waste, contamination and weaker reuse markets challenge the country’s circular economy. Recyclers are struggling with higher operating costs while demand for used textiles and recycled materials remains under pressure. Figure:The German Federation for Secondary Raw Materials and Waste Management (BVSE) is demanding a binding 30% recycled-content quota and reforms to extended producer responsibility (EPR). Germany consumes nearly 19 kg of textiles per person each year, equivalent to about 1.56 million tons of textiles annually. Around 1 million tons of textile waste are collected each year, highlighting the scale of the material flow that needs to be sorted, reused or recycled. The latest industry data shows that the quality of collected textiles has also deteriorated. Contaminants and non-textile waste in collection containers have increased from 10.8% in 2018 to between 15% and 20% today. Higher contamination makes sorting more expensive and reduces the share of material suitable for reuse or recycling. At the same time, the share of collected textiles designated for reuse fell from 62% in 2018 to 44% in 2023. Mechanical and material recycling increased to 35%, while thermal recovery, including incineration, nearly doubled from 12% to 21%. The industry is therefore calling for stronger economic incentives and policy support. The German Federation for Secondary Raw Materials and Waste Management (BVSE) is demanding a binding 30% recycled-content quota and reforms to extended producer responsibility (EPR). articles.s: Brazil ended the 2025/26 commercial year with record cotton exports, consolidating its position as the world’s largest exporter and reinforcing its role as a strategic supplier to the global textile industry. articles.x: Brazil ended the 2025/26 commercial year with record cotton exports, consolidating its position as the world’s largest exporter and reinforcing its role as a strategic supplier to the global textile industry. Between August 2025 and July 2026, the country exported 3,373,941 tonnes of cotton, an increase of 19% compared with the previous cycle. Export revenues reached a record US$5.3 billion, around 9% higher than in 2024/25, according to ComexStat data compiled by the Brazilian Association of Cotton Growers (Abrapa). The increase represents approximately 538,500 additional tonnes of Brazilian cotton sold overseas during the year. © Abrapa According to Danyella Bonfim, Market Intelligence and Analysis Coordinator at Abrapa, the performance reflects a transformation built over several years, supported by increased production and improvements in the quality, traceability and sustainability of Brazilian cotton. “Brazil has expanded its production and gained scale, while also making progress in quality, traceability and sustainability. This combination has strengthened the competitiveness of Brazilian cotton and, above all, international buyers’ confidence in the country’s ability to supply the market on a regular and consistent basis,” she said. Data from the United States Department of Agriculture, presented in Abrapa’s August report, showed Brazil maintaining its position at the top of the global cotton export rankings. The United States ranked second in 2025/26 with exports of 2.656 million tonnes, followed by Australia with 1.241 million tonnes. © Abrapa Brazil exported approximately 718,000 tonnes more than the United States, its principal competitor in the international market. articles.x: OBERTSHAUSEN, Germany — August 27, 2026 — As part of her summer tour, North Rhine-Westphalia’s Minister for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, Mona Neubaur, visited Textilfabrik 7.0 in Mönchengladbach to experience the project’s innovations first-hand. Under the motto “smart and clean”, the visit focused on innovative technologies and sustainable alternatives for textile production – from smart jackets to the decolourisation of textiles using fungal cultures. Minister Mona Neubaur with T7 logo Photo:© Tomas Rodriguez Researchers from the Research Institute for Textile and Clothing (FTB) of the Hochschule Niederrhein and the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University presented Minister Neubaur, Mönchengladbach Mayor Felix Heinrichs and representatives of state politics with innovative technologies and processes developed as part of T7. Textilfabrik 7.0 is being established in the Monforts Quartier as a real-world laboratory where innovative technologies and production processes are developed, tested under real-world conditions and further advanced for industrial application. The goal is to foster economically viable, CO₂-neutral and circular textile production in the Rhenish Mining Area. The halls of the T7-Factory in the Monforts Quartier are currently being equipped with machinery. The innovations already developed were presented to the visitors at the Technology Centre for Textile Finishing at Hochschule Niederrhein. Smart: Making Textile Production Intelligent and Digital Under the motto “smart”, the Minister explored a range of innovative technologies. articles.s: Initiative held since 2015 adopts a new format in 2026, with two immersion rounds and expanded participation from brands, retailers, NGOs and research institutes The Cotton Brazil Dialogues concludes its 2026 edition after a series of technical visits to farms, cotton gins and reference centers, as
articles.x: Initiative held since 2015 adopts a new format in 2026, with two immersion rounds and expanded participation from brands, retailers, NGOs and research institutes The Cotton Brazil Dialogues concludes its 2026 edition after a series of technical visits to farms, cotton gins and reference centers, as well as workshops focused on Brazilian cotton production. A total of 50 participants from 14 countries took part in the field trips. The initiative is led by the Brazilian Association of Cotton Growers (Abrapa) and the National Association of Cotton Exporters (Anea), with support from the Brazilian Trade and Investment Promotion Agency (ApexBrasil). Held since 2015, the initiative adopted an expanded format this year, bringing together a broader range of stakeholders from across the textile supply chain. In addition to spinners, the program welcomed representatives from brands, retailers, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), research institutes and other strategic stakeholders. Of the 50 participants, 32 represented spinning mills, while 18 represented brands, retailers and NGOs. Two immersion rounds were held in July and August. This broader participation reflects an evolution in the initiative’s approach. Beyond presenting Brazilian cotton to traditional buyers, the Cotton Brazil Dialogues creates a space for direct exchange between those who produce the fiber and those who source, transform, research, influence and make decisions across the supply chain. The aim is to foster greater understanding of Brazilian cotton production, strengthen connections between producers and the global textile industry, and contribute to a more transparent and responsible supply chain. articles.x: BUTEX Business Club has announced its new committee for the 2026–27 session, with a renewed commitment to strengthening students’ professional development, entrepreneurship, leadership skills and engagement with the corporate world. The newly formed committee aims to build on the club’s existing legacy while introducing new initiatives and platforms to create greater opportunities for students of Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). Md. Nafis Fuad, President of BUTEX Business Club, expressed his enthusiasm about taking on the leadership role, describing it as both a pleasure and a significant responsibility. Reflecting on his journey from a general member to President, he highlighted his passion for the club and his continuous desire to learn. “Leading BUTEX Business Club as its President is both an immense pleasure and a huge responsibility for me. My goal is clear: to elevate the club to new heights through our new committee, not just within the University, but across the corporate world as well,” he said. He further stated that the committee will work to serve students through new platforms and initiatives, with a focus on career development, entrepreneurship and connecting students with global opportunities. He also emphasized that the President, General Secretary and all club officials will work collectively to achieve these objectives. Abdullah Al Maruf, General Secretary of the club, said that his new responsibility represents a commitment to serve, lead and create meaningful impact. “Taking on the responsibility of General Secretary of BUTEX Business Club is an honour I deeply value. articles.t: Nanollose는 Nullarbor lyocell의 상업적 규모 확장을 목표로 합니다.
articles.o: Nanollose targets commercial scale-up of Nullarbor lyocell
articles.s: Australian biomaterials company Nanollose plans to build and operate a pilot-scale microbial cellulose pulp facility in Western Australia to accelerate the commercialization of its Nullarbor lyocell f...
articles.x: Australian biomaterials company Nanollose plans to build and operate a pilot-scale microbial cellulose pulp facility in Western Australia to accelerate the commercialization of its Nullarbor lyocell fiber. The company said the facility will help validate its microbial-cellulose production process at an industry-relevant scale. This replaces an earlier plan to develop pilot and demonstration facilities with external partners. Andrew Moullin, Managing Director, Nanollose, said the company is focusing its near-term strategy on scaling Nullarbor lyocell and proving the technology before moving toward larger commercial arrangements. After validating the process, Nanollose plans to explore licensing, joint ventures or potential sale arrangements. The company does not currently plan to invest directly in full-scale fiber manufacturing. Nullarbor produces microbial cellulose rather than conventional wood-based pulp. The technology aims to provide an alternative feedstock for regenerated cellulosic fibers such as lyocell.

articles.o: Polyester production fuels rising fashion sector emissions
articles.s: The global fashion industry’s greenhouse gas emissions rose 6.3% in 2024, after a 7.5% increase in 2023. The rise was driven largely by higher fiber production, especially polyester, according to the...
articles.x: The global fashion industry’s greenhouse gas emissions rose 6.3% in 2024, after a 7.5% increase in 2023. The rise was driven largely by higher fiber production, especially polyester, according to the Apparel Impact Institute (AII). Courtesy: Collected Fashion-sector emissions reached roughly 1 gigatons in 2024, equivalent to the total climate footprint of Japan, highlighting growing concerns over the industry’s decarbonization efforts. Kurt Kipka, Chief Impact Officer at AII, described the trend as concerning and linked the increase to greater material consumption across the industry. He also identified cost and availability as major barriers to decarbonization, noting that virgin polyester remains cheaper and more widely available than recycled alternatives. Rising energy prices are adding further pressure. Kipka said volatility caused by the Iran war underscores the need for apparel manufacturers to reduce dependence on oil and gas by adopting renewable energy and onsite battery storage. The industry could also face significant financial consequences if emissions are not reduced. Separate AII research projects a 34% decline in fashion-sector profits by 2030 due to supply-chain disruptions and rising operating costs unless companies take faster action to cut carbon emissions. Despite the challenges, the report highlighted progress in corporate climate commitments. The number of apparel companies with approved science-based climate targets or commitments to establish them increased from around 100 at the end of 2021 to more than 700 as of June 2026. Several major fashion brands have also reported double-digit emissions reductions and increased their use of recycled fibers in garments. The fabric collection is designed and created by Filo with the aim of showcasing the potential developments of the materials exhibited at the fair to Filo visitors. “M
articles.x: BIELLA, Italy — September 1, 2026 — The eagerly awaited “Made in Filo” collection is once again on show at the 66th edition of Filo. The fabric collection is designed and created by Filo with the aim of showcasing the potential developments of the materials exhibited at the fair to Filo visitors. “Made in Filo,” now in its fourth edition, is a unique initiative among international trade fairs. To implement it, Filo has taken on the challenging task of “going into production itself.” The result is a collection of fabrics created from materials provided by exhibitors, which emphasizes the technical aspects of both the yarns used and the processes employed. The project, along with Filo, involves exhibitors and several partner companies. This edition focuses on the three souls of “Botanica”, the theme of Filo66’s product development proposals, available on Filo website, filo.it. For “Spontaneous,” very simple yarns were used, but they lend a more natural feel to the fabric. “Expanded” embodies the concept of an Italian garden, with very subtle weaves and effects. “Hybridised” gives free rein to the imagination, with highly structured jacquards and much more technical yarns. The “Made in Filo” fabric collection will be exhibited at the 66th edition of Filo in an area specifically dedicated to research and innovation. A preview can be seen in this short presentation video here: https://filo.it/made-in-filo-la-collezione-di-tessuti-che-esalta-la-filiera/ The 66th edition of Filo will take place on September 15 and 16, 2026, at Fiera Milano Rho, Hall 24. Posted: September 1, 2026 Source: Filo

articles.o: SGMW industrialises bamboo fibre composites
articles.s: China’s SAIC‑GM‑Wuling (SGMW) has introduced bamboo‑fibre‑reinforced composites into interior trim components across more than 20 of its production vehicle models, covering eleven part categories including headliners, seat back panels, trunk trim, sun visors and central floor carpets. articles.x: China’s SAIC‑GM‑Wuling (SGMW) has introduced bamboo‑fibre‑reinforced composites into interior trim components across more than 20 of its production vehicle models, covering eleven part categories including headliners, seat back panels, trunk trim, sun visors and central floor carpets. In collaboration with the International Centre for Bamboo and Rattan (ICBR) and other partners, the development programme addressed three core technical areas – lightweight bamboo fibre manufacturing, fibre‑resin interface bonding and air‑flow/mechanical uniform fibre mat forming. SGMW has established a full industrial chain integrating bamboo growers, fibre processing bases, parts suppliers and vehicle assembly, and has achieved volume production of high‑performance bamboo fibre composite materials. The bamboo fibre composite is manufactured from locally sourced bamboo in Guangxi. An interfacial toughening approach using low‑melting‑point polymers improves fibre‑matrix adhesion, with stepped pressure profiles during moulding reducing void content. An air‑flow and mechanical spreading technique enables uniform mat forming for continuous production. The finished panels contain 75% or more bamboo fibre by weight, with a density around 0.5 g/cm³ which is significantly lower than conventional engineering plastics, and a flexural modulus of 257.3 MPa, meeting automotive interior requirements. A deep‑draw compression process enables forming depths exceeding 25cm, addressing the limited flowability of natural fibres in complex three‑dimensional geometries. The material exhibits near‑zero formaldehyde emissions, reduces carbon emissions by approximately 0.55 kg per kilogram of material compared with conventional plastics, and degrades more than 90% within 360 days under natural conditions. articles.x: By K. Gopalakrishnan From pioneering screen printing technologies to leading the digital printing revolution, Fujifilm Sericol India continues to shape the future of textile printing through innovation, sustainability and customer-centric solutions The textile printing industry has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past two decades. Once dominated by conventional screen printing, the industry today is rapidly embracing digital technologies, sustainable chemistries, shorter production cycles and increasingly stringent environmental regulations. Global brands are demanding not only superior print quality but also safer chemicals, lower environmental footprints, greater production flexibility and complete compliance with international sustainability standards. Dr. Raghav Rao, Managing Director, Fujifilm Sericol India Pvt. Ltd. At the heart of this transformation, inks have evolved from being merely consumables to becoming strategic enablers of innovation. Whether it is direct-to-garment (DTG), direct-to-film (DTF), sublimation, pigment or reactive printing, the chemistry behind inks today plays a defining role in determining print performance, durability, sustainability and production efficiency. As the textile printing industry continues to evolve, Fujifilm Sericol India Pvt. Ltd. has consistently remained at the forefront of this transformation. Backed by Fujifilm’s global technological leadership and Sericol’s rich heritage in printing inks, the company has spent more than 25 years helping India’s textile printers embrace new technologies while continuously introducing innovations that address the evolving needs of brands, manufacturers and consumers alike. articles.o: Successful Entry into the Coarse-Count Segment with Rieter’s Autoconer X6
articles.s: To strengthen its market position and diversify beyond commodity yarns, the company Coarser Spinning invested in an integrated Rieter ring spinning and winding solution for yarn counts Ne 4 to… The post Successful Entry into the Coarse-Count Segment with Rieter’s Autoconer X6 appeared first on The T
articles.x: To strengthen its market position and diversify beyond commodity yarns, the company Coarser Spinning invested in an integrated Rieter ring spinning and winding solution for yarn counts Ne 4 to Ne 16. The combination of ring spinning machines G 38 and Autoconer X6 winding technology enables efficient coarse-count yarn production with outstanding quality, productivity and cost efficiency. Dharmesh Patel confirms that Autoconer X6 delivers the stability and process control needed for coarse-count spinning Phenix Spinning Pvt. Ltd. founded Coarser Spinning Pvt. Ltd. in 2022 to diversify beyond the highly competitive commodity yarn market. The coarse count segment with yarn counts of Ne 4 to Ne 16 offered opportunities for differentiation and entry into more specialized applications. To succeed, the company needed a reliable and cost-efficient spinning solution capable of producing these coarse yarns with consistent quality at superior productivity. High yarn, splice and package quality were essential to support efficient downstream processing and the company’s long-term growth strategy. Building a future-ready spinning system Coarser Spinning expanded its coarse count production by investing in 10 ring spinning machines G 38 directly linked to the winding machines Autoconer X6 Type V (Fig. 1), creating an integrated Rieter spinning system. With the direct-link setup Coarser Spinning benefits from smooth material flow, high productivity and consistent yarn quality, while minimizing operator intervention. Supported by advanced winding technology, the system delivers excellent yarn, splice and package quality, providing the performance and reliability needed to establish Coarser Spinning in this market segment. articles.t: 무신사, 상반기 매출 8217억원 ‘역대 최대’…수출 9배 뛰었다
articles.o: 무신사, 상반기 매출 8217억원 ‘역대 최대’…수출 9배 뛰었다
articles.s: 무신사가 올해 상반기 8217억원 매출을 기록하며 상반기 기준 역대 최대 매출을 달성했다. 국내 오프라인 거점 확대와 글로벌 사업 성장세가 맞물리며 수출액(약 372억원)도 1년 만에 9배 이상 늘었다.무신사는 31일 2026년 상반기 연결 기준 매출이 전년 동기 대비 22.5% 증가한 8217억원을 기록했다고 밝혔다.본업 성장세가 두드러졌다. 별도 기준 매출은 7847억원으로 전년 동기 대비 30.0% 증가했다. 별도 영업이익은 657억원으로 13.1% 늘었다. 올해 상반기 주요 매출 비중은 플랫폼 입점 브랜드 중개 수수료 38%

articles.x: In a market where sustainability is fast becoming a business priority, SED’s Jodhpur conclave placed industrial water management firmly in the spotlight. As Rajasthan’s manufacturing sector faces tighter environmental norms, sustainable wastewater management has moved from compliance to competitive necessity. Against this backdrop, SED’s ZLD Jodhpur Conclave 2026 brought together industry leaders, technology experts, environmental professionals, and media for a focused discussion on the future of Zero Liquid Discharge solutions. Mr. Vimarsh Verma, Director, SED The conclave was more than a technology showcase. It created a sharp forum for dialogue on how innovation can strengthen environmental performance and operational efficiency. Strong participation from the textile, steel, and wider manufacturing sectors underscored the rising demand for practical, scalable, energy-efficient ZLD technologies. Why Jodhpur Conclave 2026 Matters for Rajasthan’s Textile Industry The conclave comes at a defining moment for Rajasthan’s textile industry. As water scarcity intensifies and compliance costs rise, efficient Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) is no longer optional; it is essential for sustainable and competitive manufacturing. The event brings industry leaders together to explore practical technologies that deliver environmental compliance without compromising commercial viability. articles.o: Don’t Stop at Fibre: The Untapped Value in Textile Recycling Wastewater
articles.s: What if the real value in textile recycling isn’t just in the fibre you recover, but also in the wastewater that can be turned into a valuable resource? Textile recycling… The post Don’t Stop at Fibre: The Untapped Value in Textile Recycling Wastewater appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
articles.x: What if the real value in textile recycling isn’t just in the fibre you recover, but also in the wastewater that can be turned into a valuable resource? Textile recycling is becoming an increasingly important part of the circular fashion conversation. Old garments are being turned into new yarn. Production waste is becoming feedstock. Fibres are getting another life. But there is an uncomfortable question the industry must ask: what happens to the water used to make that circularity possible? If recycling recovers fibre but leaves behind wastewater loaded with dyes, salts, chemicals and dissolved contaminants, the loop is not truly closed. It simply shifts waste from solid to liquid form. This is the blind spot the industry can no longer ignore. The Global Sustainability Benchmark Is Moving For textile manufacturers targeting international brands, sustainability is no longer a choice; it is a make-or-break factor. It decides who enters global supply chains and who is left behind. The Global Recycled Standard (GRS) requires 20% recycled content for certification and 50% for consumer claims , while also assessing chemical use, environmental systems, chain of custody, and social compliance. However, recycled content alone is insufficient, as broader expectations include water and resource management. Sustainability is now a baseline, not an add-on, defining long-term global competitiveness. The Hidden Water Economy Powering Circularity Textile recycling generates complex wastewater with high TDS, COD, salts, colour, hardness and chlorides. Conventional treatment focuses on safe discharge, but circular manufacturing asks: what value remains in this wastewater? articles.o: TIE technical training focuses on practical pathways to a sustainable dye house
articles.s: Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) organized a technical training under its Partnership for Implementation of Innovation Circles (PIIC) initiative on “Sustainable Dye House: Improving RFT, Reducing Re...
articles.x: Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) organized a technical training under its Partnership for Implementation of Innovation Circles (PIIC) initiative on “Sustainable Dye House: Improving RFT, Reducing Reprocessing and Lowering Water and Steam Consumption” on 23 August at the House of Textile Today in Dhaka. The training brought together professionals from Hams Group, Arien Knit Composite Ltd., Auko-Tex Group and Mondol Group, among the 16 factories participating in PIIC Season 1. Participants included dyeing laboratory and production professionals as well as GM, AGM and Assistant Manager-level representatives involved in knit dyeing operations. Figure : Technical training on Sustainable Dyehouse by TIE. The session was conducted by Rahat Ullah Rashed, Head of Technical Support, Taiwan Persotex Corporation, who has nearly 20 years of experience in the knit dyeing industry. A major focus of the training was improving Right First Time (RFT) performance to reduce reprocessing, which directly contributes to lower water, energy and chemical consumption. The session discussed laboratory preparation, lab-to-bulk correlation and bulk-to-bulk RFT, including practical limitations of laboratory dyeing compared with bulk production. Participants also explored dye combination selection, cotton dyeing techniques and differences in developing light and dark shades in bulk production. Another key area was resource efficiency. The trainer discussed opportunities for bath reduction, lower-temperature pretreatment, optimized hot washing, wash-off and rinsing. Reducing unnecessary baths can lower both water and steam consumption, supporting more efficient dye-house operations. articles.t: 퀸잇, 롯데프리미엄아울렛 동부산점과 온라인 판매 협업
articles.o: 퀸잇, 롯데프리미엄아울렛 동부산점과 온라인 판매 협업
articles.s: 4050 라이프스타일 플랫폼 퀸잇이 롯데프리미엄아울렛 동부산점과 온라인 판매 협업을 시작한다.라포랩스가 운영하는 퀸잇은 지난 5월 롯데아울렛 광교점에 이어 롯데프리미엄아울렛 동부산점 상품을 플랫폼에서 판매한다고 31일 밝혔다. 점포 기반 온라인 판매 협업으로는 두 번째 사례다.이번 협업을 통해 동부산점에 입점한 샤틴, 온앤온, 베네통, 블랙야크, 미소페 등 주요 브랜드 상품을 퀸잇에서 판매한다. 회사 측에 따르면 동부산점은 전국 아울렛 가운데 매출 2위 규모의 점포다.협업 확대에는 앞서 진행한 광교점의 온라인 판매 실적이 반영됐다.

articles.s: Première Vision Paris returns from 1-3 September 2026, bringing together nearly 900 international exhibitors and a broad range of expertise aimed at helping fashion and textile companies address rapidly changing market, technology and sustainability demands. The September edition will place particul
articles.x: Première Vision Paris returns from 1-3 September 2026, bringing together nearly 900 international exhibitors and a broad range of expertise aimed at helping fashion and textile companies address rapidly changing market, technology and sustainability demands. The September edition will place particular emphasis on its Inno-Tech theme, exploring developments reshaping product creation, manufacturing and development processes. Artificial intelligence, advanced materials, digital solutions, automation and technologies supporting more sustainable production will feature prominently. More than 900 international players will present across the show’s eight universes: Yarns, Fabrics, Designs, Accessories, Leather, Manufacturing, Smart Creation and Bag, Shoes & Leatherwear. Innovations will address areas including performance, transparency, traceability and environmental transition. Smart Creation will showcase next-generation materials including leather alternatives produced from food waste, mycelium-derived biomaterials, PLA fibres, closed-loop recycled polyesters and plant-based alternatives to fur. The area will also feature the ten winners and finalists of the 2026 ANDAM Innovation Prize, highlighting start-ups and technologies contributing to the transformation of the fashion industry. Companies presenting solutions include Hyosung, Uncaged Innovations, Dimpora, EverDye, Alterskin, SynMetabio, Peelsphere, Oleago and Sofileta. Traceability, Digital Product Passports and circularity will form another important part of the programme. Technologies will demonstrate how companies can monitor raw materials, manage certifications, improve supply chain visibility and create value from deadstock. © Première Vision Lenzing, Arvind Limited, Ipeker, A. articles.s: 국내 색사(선염사) 생산 기반이 빠르게 축소되는 가운데 목련(MOKELUN)이 고가·고품질 색사 시장의 새로운 다크호스로 떠오르고 있다.과거 국내 섬유산업의 주요 축을 형성했던 색사는 염색·방적업체들의 생산기반 축소와 인건비 및 생산비 상승 등으로 국내 생산 물량이 크게 줄어든 상황이다.특히 다품종 소량 생산과 빠른 납기를 요구하는 패션시장의 수요에 비해 국내 공급 기반이 취약해지면서 고품질 색사를 안정적으로 공급할 수 있는 전문업체의 중요성이 높아지고 있다.이 같은 시장 변화 속에서 목련이 차별화된 경쟁력을 앞세워 고가 색사 시장

articles.s: 대구염색산업 단지 내 중견 염색 가공 업체인 ㈜청운다이텍(대표 하영도)이 공장 가동을 포기한 것으로 알려졌다.중견 폴리에스테르 감량 가공 전문 회사인 청운다이텍은 갈수록 가공물량 급감으로 경영 환경이 위기에 몰리자 결국 사업을 포기하는 극단적인 결정을 내렸다는 것이다.대구염색산지내 2차 단지에 소재한 이 회사는 거래 직물 업체에 “8월 말까지 공장을 가동하고 업을 접겠다”고 통보한 것으로 알려졌다.코로나 이후 거듭되는 수출 경기 악화로 가공물량이 고갈되자 가동률 30~40%에 머문 염색산단 입주 기업의 어려움을 반영하듯 청운다이텍이

articles.t: 하고하우스, 브랜드 아닌 ‘착장’을 판다…여성 편집숍 ‘리포먼트’ 출격
articles.o: 하고하우스, 브랜드 아닌 ‘착장’을 판다…여성 편집숍 ‘리포먼트’ 출격
articles.s: 하고하우스가 브랜드별로 상품을 나열하던 기존 편집숍의 공식을 깨고 ‘착장’을 전면에 내세운 새로운 여성 디자이너 편집숍을 선보인다.국내 대표 브랜드 인큐베이터 하고하우스는 여성 디자이너 브랜드 전문 편집숍 ‘리포먼트(REFORMENT)’를 론칭하고 현대백화점 판교점과 롯데백화점 잠실점에 잇따라 매장을 열었다. 리포먼트는 여러 브랜드의 상품을 하나의 스타일로 조합해 보여주는 ‘스타일 중심 큐레이션’을 핵심 경쟁력으로 내세운다.기존 편집숍이 브랜드별 공간과 상품 진열을 중심으로 운영됐다면 리포먼트는 브랜드 간 경계를 허문 것이 특징이다

articles.t: [26상반기 실적] 상반기 면방 경기 소문대로 좋았다
articles.o: [26상반기 실적] 상반기 면방 경기 소문대로 좋았다
articles.s: 지난 4~5년간 침체기였던 면방 경기가 올 상반기에 기사 회생해 흑자 행진을 만끽한 것으로 나타났다.12월 결산 면방 상장사들의 올 상반기 경영 실적이 대부분 호황을 누린 것으로 드러났다.면방 상장사 중 경방은 상반기 중 매출 2281억2600만 원, 영업 이익 756억9300만 원을 달성해 작년 동기 대비 매출은 15.6% 증가한 데 비해 영업 이익은 24%나 늘어났다.물론 경방은 유통업체 타임스퀘어의 안정적인 성장이 크게 기여했지만 면방 경기가 올 상반기 중 활황을 유지한 결과물로 분석되고 있다.일신방은 올 상반기 매출 2790

articles.s: 글로벌 면화시장에서 가격과 섬유 품질에 더해 원산지와 공급망 이력을 입증하는 능력이 새로운 경쟁요소로 부상하고 있다. 미국은 농장에서 최종 제품까지 면화의 이동 경로를 확인하는 시스템을 확대하고 있고, 피지컬 베터코튼의 실물 기반 이력관리 체계는 15개 생산국으로 넓어졌다. 인도 역시 국가 면화 브랜드에 QR코드와 블록체인을 적용하고 있다.미국에서는 ‘U.S. 코튼 트러스트 프로토콜(U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol)’을 중심으로 이력관리가 확대되고 있다. 2024~2025 연차보고서에 따르면 20개 브랜드가 약 12

articles.s: 한국아웃도어스포츠산업협회(회장 임석원, 이하 협회)가 오는 8월 19일부터 21일까지 서울 코엑스에서 열리는 국내 최대 규모 섬유패션 소재 전시회 『PIS(프리뷰인서울) 2026』에 참가한다.이번 참가는 산업통상부가 지원하고 협회가 주관하는 「섬유패션 수요-제조간 AI활용 디지털 공급망 구축사업」(이하 섬기력사업)의 국내전시 지원 프로그램 일환으로, 사업 수혜기업을 대상으로 마련된 자리다. 협회는 코엑스 더 플라츠(2F)에 전시 기간 부스를 운영하며 섬유패션 AI 매칭 플랫폼 시연, 수혜기업 41개사 소개·의류 전시, 글로벌 트레이

articles.t: 러 공습 ‘푸마’ 물류창고 파괴
articles.o: 러 공습 ‘푸마’ 물류창고 파괴
articles.s: 러시아의 공습으로 스포츠 브랜드 푸마가 우크라이나에서 사용하던 물류창고가 파괴됐다. 직원 인명피해는 없었지만 재고와 물류장비가 소실되면서 일부 제품의 공급과 배송에 차질이 예상된다.피해가 발생한 곳은 수도 키이우 인근 차이카에 위치한 덴카로지스틱스 물류단지다. 푸마는 이곳을 우크라이나 내 상품 보관과 유통을 위한 물류 거점으로 이용해왔다. 이번 공격으로 창고가 피해를 입으면서 회사는 공급망 복구에 나섰다.푸마는 물류망을 정상화하는 과정에서 일부 상품의 재고가 일시적으로 부족할 수 있다고 밝혔다. 직원들은 모두 안전한 것으로 알려졌다

articles.t: 럭셔리 회복 온도차…샤넬↑ 마이클코어스↓
articles.o: 럭셔리 회복 온도차…샤넬↑ 마이클코어스↓
articles.s: 글로벌 럭셔리 · 프리미엄 패션 시장에서 브랜드별 실적이 엇갈렸다. 샤넬과 랄프로렌은 미국과 중국 등 주요 시장에서 두 자릿수 성장률을 기록한 반면 마이클코어스는 매출 감소세를 이어갔다.블룸버그가 소식통을 인용해 보도한 바에 따르면 샤넬의 2026년 상반기 동일 기준 매출은 전년 동기보다 약 16% 증가했다. 마티유 블라지 크리에이티브 디렉터의 첫 컬렉션 출시와 미국 판매 호조가 성장을 이끈 것으로 전해졌다. 전체 매출의 약 60%를 차지하는 패션 사업도 비슷한 성장세를 보였다. 시계 · 파인주얼리 매출은 35% 늘었다. 미국 매출

articles.t: 8월 폭염인데… 벌써 ‘경량패딩’ 열풍
articles.o: 8월 폭염인데… 벌써 ‘경량패딩’ 열풍
articles.s: 폭염이 지속되는 이달 때아닌 경량패딩 판매 열풍이 한창이다.지난해 11월부터 불어닥친 한파를 경험한 소비자들이 이달 얼리버드로 경량패딩 신상품이 풀리자 구매 열풍이 확산되고 있다. 무신사는 한여름임에도 경량패딩을 찾는 고객들의 반응이 뜨겁게 나타나고 있다고 밝히며 8월 1일부터 10일까지 무신사 내 ‘경량패딩’ 검색량은 전년 동기 대비 105% 증가했다고 알렸다. 이에 제도권 아웃도어 브랜드들도 무신사 랭킹 선점을 위해 온라인 집중 전략을 펼치고 있다는 소식. 입점사들은 단독 기획 경량패딩, 선제적 프로모션 등 주도권 확보 싸움이

articles.o: 케이비엘러먼트, 사용 편의성 강화한 ‘그래핀 마스터배치’ 사업 본격 확대
articles.s: 비산화 그래핀 양산 기업 케이비엘러먼트(KB-ELEMENT, 대표 배경정)가 ‘그래핀 마스터배치’ 사업을 본격 확대한다. 기존 제조 공정에 바로 적용할 수 있는 사용 편의성을 앞세워 그래핀 응용 분야를 확장하겠다는 전략이다.그래핀은 우수한 강도, 전기전도성, 열전도성을 가진 소재이지만 높은 가격과 분산 난제로 ‘꿈의 소재’에 머물러 있었다. 케이비엘러먼트는 대기압 플라즈마 공법의 비산화 그래핀 양산에 성공해 원가 경쟁력을 확보했다. 이어 그래핀 마스터배치를 통해 분산의 기술적 한계를 해결하며 그래핀 상용화에 새로운 전환점을 제시한다

articles.s: 경기도 양주 소재 날염 전처리 가공 전문 업체인 유림섬유(대표 임택기)에서 지난 6일 대형 화재가 발생해 보관 중인 원단 상당량이 소실되는 피해를 입었다.이날 불은 오후 6시 16분쯤 발화돼 공장 내에 보관 중인 생지중 상당부문을 태우고 가까스로 진화됐다.관할 소방 당국에 따르면 양주시 봉양동 356-8 소재 유림섬유에서 발생 된 대형 화재로 보관 중인 원단 일부를 태운 것은 물론 사망 사고는 없는 대신 연기 흡연 1명, 찰과상 3명 등 4명의 부상자가 발생했다.정확한 재산 피해는 확인중이다.이 회사는 경기 북부 지역에 유일하게 남

articles.s: 심장 · 혈관 수술이 카테터를 이용한 최소 침습 방식으로 전환되면서 의료용 직물도 더 얇고 작 으면서 높은 강도를 유지하는 방향으로 진화하 고 있다. 좁은 카테터 안에 들어가면서 장기간 물 리적 하중을 견뎌야해 정밀 제직 기술의 중요성이 커지는 추세다.업계에서는 10~20데니어 수준의 극세사를 활용해 혈관 이식재와 심장판막 부품의 부피를 줄 이는 기술을 개발하고 있다. 폴리에스터(PET)와 초고분자량폴리에틸렌(UHMWPE) 계열 고강도 섬유등이 주요 소재로 활용된다.원사가 가늘어질수록 제직 과정에서 마찰과 력에 따른 손상 위험이 커
